<b><a id="_2_06">*2·06</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp p \supset q . \supset \colon q \supset r . \supset . p \supset r\)" src="images/784.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 26.388ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_784.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \left[\text{Comm} \frac{q \supset r, p \supset q, p \supset r}{p,\,\,\, q,\,\,\, r}\right] &amp;\vdash \colon\colon q \supset r . \supset \colon p \supset q . \supset . p \supset r \colon\ldotp\\ &amp;\supset \colon\ldotp p \supset q . \supset \colon q \supset r . \supset . p \supset r \qquad \text{(1)}\\ [\text{*2·05}] &amp;\vdash \colon\ldotp q \supset r . \supset \colon p \supset q . \supset . p \supset r \qquad \text{(2)}\\ [\text{(1).(2).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash \colon\ldotp p \supset q . \supset \colon q \supset r . \supset . p \supset r \end{array} \]" src="images/785.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.221ex; width: 55.258ex; height: 13.572ex;" id="img_images_785.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_105">[Pg 105]</span></p>

<p>In the last line of this proof, "(1).(2).*1·11" means that we are
inferring in accordance with <a href="#_1_11" class="pginternal">*1·11</a>, having before us a proposition,
namely <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\supset q\ldotp \supset :q\supset r\ldotp\supset \ldotp p\supset r\)" src="images/786.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 23.245ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_786.svg">,
which, by (1), is implied by <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\supset r\ldotp\supset :p\supset q\ldotp\supset \ldotp p\supset r\)" src="images/787.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 23.245ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_787.svg">,
which, by (2), is true. In general, in such cases, we shall omit
the reference to *1·11.</p>

<p>The above two propositions will both be referred to as the "principle
of the syllogism" (shortened to "Syll"), because, as will appear later,
the syllogism in Barbara is derived from them.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*2·07</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p\ldotp\supset \ldotp p\lor p \quad\left[\text{*1·3}\, \frac{p}{q}\right]\)" src="images/788.svg" style="vertical-align: -1.469ex; width: 23.317ex; height: 4.07ex;" id="img_images_788.svg"></p>

<p>Here we put nothing beyond "*1·3 <img alt="" data-tex="\(\dfrac{p}{q}\)" src="images/789.svg" style="vertical-align: -1.991ex; width: 2.133ex; height: 4.52ex;" id="img_images_789.svg">," because the
proposition to be proved is what <a href="#_1_3" class="pginternal">*1·3</a> becomes when <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_206"> is written in
place of <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_134">.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*2·08</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\ldotp p\supset p\)" src="images/790.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.681ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_790.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} {\Large [}\text{*2·05} \frac{p\lor p,p}{q,r}{\Large ]} &amp;\vdash\colon\colon p\lor p\ldotp\supset \ldotp p:\supset \colon\ldotp p\ldotp\supset \ldotp p\lor p:\supset \ldotp p\supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ [\text{Taut}] &amp;\vdash:p\lor p\ldotp\supset \ldotp p &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ [\text{(1).(2).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash\colon\ldotp p\ldotp\supset \ldotp p\lor p:\supset \ldotp p\supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ [\text{2·07}] &amp;\vdash:p\ldotp\supset \ldotp p\lor p &amp;\qquad \text{(4)}\\ [\text{(3).(4).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash\ldotp p\supset p \end{array} \]" src="images/791.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.536ex; width: 62.536ex; height: 16.204ex;" id="img_images_791.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">

<p>This is the law of excluded middle.</p>

the principle of double negation.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \left[\text{Sum}\, \frac{{\sim}p{\sim}\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)\}}}{q,\,\,\,\,r}\right] &amp;\vdash \colon\ldotp{\sim}p.\supset.\sim\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)\}}.\supset \colon p \lor {\sim}p.\supset.p \lor {\sim}\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)\}} &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \left[\text{*2·12} \quad \frac{{\sim}p}{p}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon:{\sim}p.\supset.{\sim}\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)}\} &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ [\text{(1).(2).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash\colon p\lor{\sim}p.\supset.p\lor{\sim}\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)\}} &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ [\text{(3).*2·11.*1·11}] &amp;\vdash\colon p\lor{\sim}\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)\}} \end{array} \]" src="images/798.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.124ex; width: 78.607ex; height: 15.38ex;" id="img_images_798.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \left[\text{Perm}\, \frac{{\sim}\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)\}}}{q}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon p \lor {\sim}\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)\}}.\supset.{\sim}\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)\}}\lor p &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ [\text{(1).*2·13.*1·11}] &amp;\vdash\colon{\sim}\{{{\sim}({\sim}p)\}} \lor p &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ [\text{(2).(*1·01)}] &amp;\vdash\colon{\sim}({\sim}p)\supset p \end{array} \]" src="images/800.svg" style="vertical-align: -4.637ex; width: 62.498ex; height: 10.405ex;" id="img_images_800.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_2_15">*2·15</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon {\sim}p \supset q.\supset.{\sim}q \supset p\)" src="images/801.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 20.073ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_801.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \left[\text{*2·05}\, \frac{{\sim}p,{\sim}({\sim}q)}{p,\,\,\,r}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon\ldotp q\supset{\sim}({\sim}q).\supset\colon{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}p\supset{\sim}({\sim}q) &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \left[\text{*2·12}\, \frac{q}{p}\right]&amp; \vdash\colon q \supset{\sim}({\sim}q) \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad &amp;\qquad\text{(2)}\\ [\text{(1).(2).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash\colon\supset {\sim}p.\supset.q.\supset.{\sim}p\supset {\sim}({\sim}q) &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \left[\text{*2·03}\, \frac{{\sim}p,{\sim}q}{p,\,\,\,q}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon{\sim}p\supset{\sim}({\sim}q).\supset.{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p) &amp;\qquad \text{(4)}\\ \left[\text{*2·05}\, \frac{{\sim}q,{\sim}({\sim}p)}{p,\,\,q,\,\,r}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon\ldotp{\sim}({\sim}p)\supset p.\supset\colon{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p).\supset.{\sim}q\supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(5)}\\ q,{\sim}p\supset{\sim}({\sim}q),{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p)}{p,\,\,\,q,\,\,\,r}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon\colon\\ \qquad\qquad\qquad&amp;{\sim}p\supset{\sim}({\sim}q).\supset.{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p)\colon\supset\colon\ldotp\\ \qquad\qquad\qquad&amp;{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}p\supset{\sim}({\sim}q)\colon\supset\colon{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p) \qquad &amp;\qquad\text{(7)}\\ [(\text{4).(7).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash\colon\ldotp{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}p\supset{\sim}({\sim}q)\colon\supset\colon\\ \qquad\qquad\qquad&amp;{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p) \qquad &amp;\qquad\text{(8)}\\ [\text{(3).(8).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash:{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p) &amp;\qquad \text{(9)}\\ \left[\text{*2·05}\, \frac{{\sim}p\supset q,{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p),{\sim}q\supset p}{p,\,\,q,\,\,r}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon\colon{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p).\supset.{\sim}q\supset p:\\ &amp;\supset\colon\ldotp{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p):\supset:{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}q\supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(10)}\\ [\text{(6).(10).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash\colon\ldotp{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}q\supset{\sim}({\sim}p):\supset:\\ \qquad\qquad\qquad&amp;{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}q\supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(11)}\\ [\text{(9).(11).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash:{\sim}p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}q\supset p \end{array} \]" src="images/802.svg" style="vertical-align: -31.328ex; width: 96.597ex; height: 63.787ex;" id="img_images_802.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_107">[Pg 107]</span></p>

<p><i>Note on the proof of</i> <a href="#_2_15" class="pginternal">*2·15</a>. In the above proof, it will be
seen that (3), (4), (6) are respectively of the forms <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{1}\supset p_{2}\)" src="images/803.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_803.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{2}\supset p_{3}\)" src="images/804.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_804.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{3}\supset p_{4}\)" src="images/805.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_805.svg">, where
<img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{1}\supset p_{4}\)" src="images/806.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_806.svg"> is the proposition to be proved. From
<img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{1}\supset p_{2}\)" src="images/803.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_803.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{2}\supset p_{3}\)" src="images/804.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_804.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{3}\supset p_{4}\)" src="images/805.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_805.svg_1">
the proposition <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{1}\supset p_{4}\)" src="images/806.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_806.svg_1"> results by repeated applications
of <a href="#_2_05" class="pginternal">*2·05</a> or <a href="#_2_06" class="pginternal">*2·06</a> (both of which are called "Syll"). It is tedious
and unnecessary to repeat this process every time it is used; it will
therefore be abbreviated into
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \unicode{x201c}[\text{Syll}]\, \vdash.(a).(b).(c).\supset \vdash.(d),\unicode{x201d} \]" src="images/807.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 30.162ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_807.svg"></span>
where (<i>a</i>) is of the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{1}\supset p_{2}\)" src="images/803.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_803.svg_2">, (<i>b</i>) of
the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{2}\supset p_{3}\)" src="images/804.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_804.svg_2">, (<i>c</i>) of the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{3}\supset p_{4}\)" src="images/805.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_805.svg_2">,
and (<i>d</i>) of the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{1}\supset p_{4}\)" src="images/806.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_806.svg_2">. The same
abbreviation will be applied to a sorites of any length.</p>

<p>Also where we have "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.p_{1}\)" src="images/808.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 4.514ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_808.svg">" and "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.p_{1}\supset p_{2}\)" src="images/809.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 9.657ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_809.svg">,"
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{2}\)" src="images/810.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.126ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_810.svg"> is the proposition to be proved, it is
convenient to write simply
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \unicode{x201c}&amp;\vdash.p_{1}.\supset\\ [\text{etc}.]\qquad &amp;\vdash.p_{2},\unicode{x201d} \end{array} \]" src="images/811.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.149ex; width: 19.221ex; height: 5.43ex;" id="img_images_811.svg"></span>
where "etc." will be a reference to the previous propositions in
virtue of which the implication "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p_{1}\supset p_{2}\)" src="images/803.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.268ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_803.svg_3">" holds. This
form embodies the use of <a href="#_1_11" class="pginternal">*1·11</a> or <a href="#_1_1" class="pginternal">*1·1</a>, and makes many proofs at once
shorter and easier to follow. It is used in the first two lines of the
following proof.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_2_16">*2·16</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon p\supset q.\supset .{\sim}q\supset {\sim}p\)" src="images/812.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 20.073ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_812.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} [\text{*2·12}] &amp;\vdash.q\supset{\sim}({\sim}q).\supset\\ [\text{*2·05}] &amp;\vdash\colon p\supset q.\supset.p\supset {\sim}({\sim}q) &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \left[\text{*2·03}\, \frac{{\sim}q}{q}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon p{\sim}({\sim}q).\supset.{\sim}q\supset{\sim}p &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ [\text{Syll}] &amp;\vdash.(1).(2).\supset\vdash\colon p\supset q.\supset.{\sim}q\supset{\sim}p \end{array} \]" src="images/813.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.221ex; width: 54.601ex; height: 13.572ex;" id="img_images_813.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_108">[Pg 108]</span></p>

<p><i>Note.</i> The proposition to be proved will be called
"Prop," and when a proof ends, like that of <a href="#_2_16" class="pginternal">*2·16</a>, by an
implication between asserted propositions, of which the
consequent is the proposition to be proved, we shall write
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\text{etc}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop}\)" src="images/814.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 15.249ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_814.svg">". Thus
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\supset\vdash.\text{Prop}\)" src="images/815.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 8.965ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_815.svg">" ends a proof, and more or less
corresponds to "<span class="allsmcap">Q.E.D.</span>"</p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_2_17">*2·17</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon {\sim}q\supset{\sim}p.\supset.p\supset q\)" src="images/816.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 20.073ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_816.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \left[\text{*2·03} \frac{{\sim}q\, p}{p,\,\,q}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon{\sim}q\supset{\sim}p.\supset.p\supset{\sim}({\sim}q) &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ [\text{*2·14}] &amp;\vdash\colon{\sim}({\sim}q)\supset q\colon \supset\\ [\text{*2·05}] &amp;\vdash\colon p\supset{\sim}({\sim}q).\supset.p\supset q &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ [\text{Syll}] &amp;\vdash.(1).(2).\supset\vdash.\, \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/817.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.221ex; width: 48.742ex; height: 13.572ex;" id="img_images_817.svg"></span></p>

<p><a href="#_2_15" class="pginternal">*2·15</a>, <a href="#_2_16" class="pginternal">*2·16</a> and <a href="#_2_17" class="pginternal">*2·17</a> are forms of the principle of transposition, and
will be all referred to as "Transp."</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*2·18.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon{\sim}p\supset p.\supset.p\)" src="images/818.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 14.352ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_818.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} [\text{*2·12}] &amp;\vdash.p\supset{\sim}({\sim}p).\supset\\ [\text{*2·05}] &amp;\vdash.{\sim}p\supset p.\supset.{\sim}p\supset{\sim}({\sim}p) &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \left[\text{*2·01} \frac{{\sim}p}{p}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon{\sim}p\supset{\sim}({\sim}p).\supset.{\sim}({\sim}p) &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ [\text{Syll}] &amp;\vdash.(1).(2).\supset \vdash\colon{\sim}p\supset p.\supset.{\sim}({\sim}p) &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ [\text{*2·14}] &amp;\vdash.{\sim}({\sim}p)\supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(4)}\\ [\text{Syll}] &amp;\vdash.(3).(4).\supset\vdash.\, \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/819.svg" style="vertical-align: -9.388ex; width: 53.851ex; height: 19.907ex;" id="img_images_819.svg"></span></p>

<p>This is the complement of the principle of the <i>reductio ad
absurdum</i>. It states that a proposition which follows from the
hypothesis of its own falsehood is true.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{Add}.\supset \vdash\colon p.\supset.q \lor p &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ [\text{Perm}]\vdash\colon q \lor p.\supset.p \lor q &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ [\text{Syll}]\vdash.(1).(2).\supset\vdash.\, \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/821.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.733ex; width: 34.802ex; height: 8.597ex;" id="img_images_821.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_2_31">*2·31</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon p \lor (q \lor r).\supset.(p \lor q) \lor r\)" src="images/830.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.138ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_830.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition and <a href="#_2_32" class="pginternal">*2·32</a> together constitute the associative law
for logical addition of propositions. In the proof, the following
abbreviation (constantly used hereafter) will be employed<a class="fnanchor pginternal" href="#Footnote_47" id="FNanchor_47">[47]</a>: When we
have a series of propositions of the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(a \supset b\)" src="images/831.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 5.185ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_831.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(b \supset c\)" src="images/832.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 4.967ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_832.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(c \supset d\)" src="images/833.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 5.173ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_833.svg">, all asserted, and "<img alt="" data-tex="\(a \supset d\)" src="images/834.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 5.39ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_834.svg">" is the
proposition to be proved, the proof in full is as follows:</p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} &amp;[\text{Syll}] &amp;\vdash \colon\ldotp a\supset b.\supset \colon b\supset c.\supset.a\supset c &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ &amp;&amp;\vdash \colon.\supset.b &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ &amp;[\text{(1).(2).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash \colon b \supset c.\supset.a\supset c &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ &amp;&amp;\vdash \colon b.\supset.c &amp;\qquad \text{(4)}\\ &amp;[\text{(3).(4).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash \colon a.\supset.c &amp;\qquad \text{(5)}\\ &amp;[\text{Syll}] &amp;\vdash \colon\ldotp a\supset c.\supset\colon c\supset d.\supset.a \supset d &amp;\qquad \text{(6)}\\ &amp;[\text{(5).(6).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash \colon c\supset d.\supset.a\supset d &amp;\qquad \text{(7)}\\ &amp;&amp;\vdash \colon c.\supset.d &amp;\qquad \text{(8)}\\ &amp;[\text{(7).(8).*1·11}] &amp;\vdash \colon a.\supset.d \end{array} \]" src="images/835.svg" style="vertical-align: -13.235ex; width: 54.352ex; height: 27.602ex;" id="img_images_835.svg"></span></p>

<p>It is tedious to write out this process in full; we therefore write
simply</p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} &amp;\vdash \colon a.\supset.b.\\ &amp;[\text{etc.}]\,\supset.c.\\ &amp;[\text{etc.}]\,\supset.d:\supset\vdash.\text{Prop}, \end{array} \]" src="images/836.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.733ex; width: 22.839ex; height: 8.597ex;" id="img_images_836.svg"></span>
where "<img alt="" data-tex="\(a \supset d\)" src="images/834.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 5.39ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_834.svg_1">" is the proposition to be proved. We indicate on
the left by references in square brackets the propositions in virtue
of which the successive implications hold. We put one dot (not two)
after "<img alt="" data-tex="\(b\)" src="images/181.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 0.971ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_181.svg_19">," to show<span class="pagenum" id="Page_110">[Pg 110]</span> that it is <img alt="" data-tex="\(b\)" src="images/181.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 0.971ex; height: 1.595ex;" id="img_images_181.svg_20">, not "<img alt="" data-tex="\(a\supset b\)" src="images/837.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 5.185ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_837.svg">," that
implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(c\)" src="images/319.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 0.98ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_319.svg_17">. But we put two dots after <img alt="" data-tex="\(d\)" src="images/838.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.176ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_838.svg">, to show that now the
whole proposition "<img alt="" data-tex="\(a\supset d\)" src="images/839.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 5.39ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_839.svg">" is concerned. If "<img alt="" data-tex="\(a\supset d\)" src="images/839.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 5.39ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_839.svg_1">" is
not the proposition to be proved, but is to be used subsequently in the
proof, we put</p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash\colon a.\supset.b.\\ [\text{etc.}]\supset.c.\\ [\text{etc.}]\supset.d &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}, \end{array} \]" src="images/840.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.733ex; width: 20.087ex; height: 8.597ex;" id="img_images_840.svg"></span>
and then "(1)" means "<img alt="" data-tex="\(a\supset d.\)" src="images/841.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 6.019ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_841.svg">" The proof of <a href="#_2_31" class="pginternal">*2·31</a> is as follows:</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} [\text{*2·3}] \vdash\colon p \lor (q\lor r).&amp;\supset.p \lor(r \lor q).\\ \left[\text{Assoc}\, \frac{r,\,q}{q,\,r}\right] &amp;\supset.r \lor (p \lor q).\\ \left[\text{Perm}\, \frac{r,\,p \lor q}{p,\,q}\right] &amp;\supset.(p \lor q) \lor r \colon\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/842.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.541ex; width: 43.903ex; height: 12.213ex;" id="img_images_842.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \left[\text{Perm}\, \frac{p \lor q,\,r}{p,\,q}\right] \vdash\colon(p \lor q)\lor r.&amp;\supset.r \lor (p\lor q)\\ \left[\text{Assoc}\, \frac{r,\,p,\,q}{p,\,q,\,r}\right] &amp;\supset.p \lor(r \lor q)\\ [\text{*2·3}] &amp;\supset.p \lor (q \lor r)\colon\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/844.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.541ex; width: 51.6ex; height: 12.213ex;" id="img_images_844.svg"></span></p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} [\text{Perm}] &amp;\vdash\colon p\ lor r.\supset.r \lor p\colon\\ \left[\text{Syll} \frac{p \lor q,\,p \lor r,\,r \lor p}{p,\,q,\,r}\right] &amp;\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp p\lor q.\supset.p\lor r\colon\supset\colon p \lor q.\supset.r \lor p &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ [Sum] &amp;\vdash\colon\ldotp p q\supset r.\supset\colon p \lor q.\supset.p\lor r &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).(2).Syll}.\supset\vdash.\, \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/847.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.221ex; width: 70.634ex; height: 13.572ex;" id="img_images_847.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_111">[Pg 111]</span></p>

<p>The proofs of *2·37·38 are exactly analogous to that of <a href="#_2_36" class="pginternal">*2·36</a>. (We use
"*2·37·38" as an abbreviation for "<a href="#_2_37" class="pginternal">*2·37</a> and <a href="#_2_38" class="pginternal">*2·38</a>." Such abbreviations
will be used throughout.)</p>

<p>The use of a general principle of deduction, such as either form
of "Syll," in a proof, is different from the use of the particular
premisses to which the principle of deduction is applied. The principle
of deduction gives the general rule according to which the inference is
made, but is not itself a premiss in the inference. If we treated it
as a premiss, we should need either it or some other general rule to
enable us to infer the desired conclusion, and thus we should gradually
acquire an increasing accumulation of premisses without ever being able
to make any inference. Thus when a general rule is adduced in drawing
an inference, as when we write "<img alt="" data-tex="\([\text{Syll}]\vdash.(1).(2).\supset \vdash.\text{Prop},\)" src="images/850.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 25.374ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_850.svg">" the mention of "Syll" is only required in order
to remind the reader how the inference is drawn.</p>

<p>The rule of inference may, however, also occur as one of the ordinary
premisses, that is to say, in the case of "Syll" for example, the
proposition "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\supset q.\supset \colon q\supset r.\supset.p\supset r\)" src="images/851.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 22.994ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_851.svg">"
may be one of those to which our rules of deduction are applied,
and it is then an ordinary premiss. The distinction between the two
uses of principles of deduction is of some philosophical importance,
and in the above proofs we have indicated it by putting the rule of
inference in square brackets. It is, however, practically inconvenient
to continue to distinguish in the manner of the reference. We shall
therefore henceforth both adduce ordinary premisses in square brackets
where convenient, and adduce rules of inference, along with other
propositions, in asserted premisses, <i>i.e.</i> we shall write
<i>e.g.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} &amp;\unicode{x201c}\vdash.(1).(2).\text{Syll}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop}\unicode{x201d}\\ \text{rather than}\qquad &amp;\unicode{x201c}\text{Syll}\vdash.(1).(2).\supset\vdash.\text{Prop}\unicode{x201d} \end{array} \]" src="images/852.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.149ex; width: 44.684ex; height: 5.43ex;" id="img_images_852.svg"></span></p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \left[\text{*2·67} \frac{{\sim}p}{p}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\supset.q\colon\supset.{\sim}p\supset q \qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.(1).\text{*2·54}.&amp;\supset\vdash.\text{Prop}\\ \end{array} \]" src="images/884.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.053ex; width: 45.879ex; height: 7.238ex;" id="img_images_884.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*2·69.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\supset.q\colon\supset\colon q\supset p.\supset.p \quad\left[\text{*2·68.Perm.*2·62}\, \frac{q,\,p}{p,\,q}\right]\)" src="images/885.svg" style="vertical-align: -1.469ex; width: 52.676ex; height: 4.07ex;" id="img_images_885.svg"></p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*2·53.Perm}.\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp q\lor r.&amp;\supset\colon{\sim}r\supset q\colon\\ [\text{*2·38}] &amp;\supset\colon{\sim}r\lor s.\supset.q\lor s\colon\ldotp \supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/892.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.149ex; width: 55.604ex; height: 5.43ex;" id="img_images_892.svg"></span></p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{Sum}.\supset\vdash\colon\colon q.\supset.r\supset s\colon\supset\colon\ldotp &amp;p\lor q.\supset\colon p.\lor.r\supset s &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{*2·76.Syll}.\supset\vdash\colon\colon p\lor q.\supset\colon&amp; p.\lor.r\supset s\colon\ldotp\supset\colon\ldotp\\ &amp;p\lor q.\supset\colon p\lor r.\supset.p\lor s &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).(2)}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/894.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 60.828ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_894.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} [\text{Add.Syll}] \vdash\colon\ldotp p\lor q.&amp;\supset.r\colon\supset.q\supset r &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{*2·55}.\supset\vdash\colon\colon{\sim}p.&amp;\supset\colon\ldotp p\lor r.\supset.r\colon\ldotp\\ [\text{Syll}] &amp;\supset\colon\ldotp p\lor q.\supset.p\lor r\colon\supset\colon p\lor q.\supset.r\colon\ldotp\\ [\text{(1).*2·83}] \supset\colon\ldotp p\lor q.\supset.&amp;p\lor r\colon\supset\colon q\supset r &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.(2).\text{Comm}.\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp &amp;p\lor q.\supset.p \lor r\colon\supset\colon{\sim}p.\supset.q\supset r\colon\\ [\text{*2·54}] &amp;\supset\colon p.\lor.q\supset r\colon\ldotp\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/898.svg" style="vertical-align: -8.484ex; width: 66.166ex; height: 18.1ex;" id="img_images_898.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*2·86.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\supset.p\supset r\colon\supset\colon p.\supset.q\supset r \quad\left[\text{*2·85}\, \frac{{\sim}p}{p}\right]\)" src="images/899.svg" style="vertical-align: -1.469ex; width: 44.65ex; height: 4.07ex;" id="img_images_899.svg"></p>

propositions applies with even greater force to primitive ideas.</p>

mean that it can be expressed in terms of the primitive ideas of logic.

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_114">[Pg 114]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_3">*3. THE LOGICAL PRODUCT OF TWO PROPOSITIONS.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *3.</p>

<p>The logical product of two propositions <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_207"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_135"> is practically
the proposition "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_208"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_136"> are both true." But this as it stands
would have to be a new primitive idea. We therefore take as the logical
product the proposition <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}({\sim}p\lor {\sim}q)\)" src="images/900.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.734ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_900.svg">, <i>i.e.</i>
"it is false that either <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_209"> is false or <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_137"> is false," which is
obviously true when and only when <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_210"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_138"> are both true. Thus
we put</p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_3_01">*3·01</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(p.q .=. {\sim}({\sim}p \lor {\sim}q) \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/901.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 23.374ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_901.svg"></p>

<p>where "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p . q\)" src="images/75.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 3.185ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_75.svg_4">" is the logical product of <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_211"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_139">.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_3_02">*3·02</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(p \supset q \supset r.=. p \supset q . q \supset r \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/902.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 28.969ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_902.svg"></p>

<p>This definition serves merely to abbreviate proofs.</p>

<p>When we are given two asserted propositional functions "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \ldotp{\phi}x\)" src="images/903.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 5.031ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_903.svg">"
and "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \ldotp {\psi}x\)" src="images/904.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 5.155ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_904.svg">," we shall have "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\ldotp {\phi}x \ldotp {\psi}x\)" src="images/905.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 8.804ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_905.svg">"
whenever <img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi\)" src="images/55.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.348ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_55.svg_40"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\psi\)" src="images/56.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.473ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_56.svg_10"> take arguments of the same type. This
will be proved for any functions in *9; for the present, we are
confined to <i>elementary</i> propositional functions of elementary
propositions. In this case, the result is proved as follows:</p>

<p>By <a href="#_1_7" class="pginternal">*1·7</a>, <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}{\phi}p\)" src="images/906.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.247ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_906.svg"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}{\psi}p\)" src="images/907.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.371ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_907.svg"> are elementary
propositional functions, and therefore, by <a href="#_1_72" class="pginternal">*1·72</a>, <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}{\phi}p \lor{\sim}{\psi}p\)" src="images/908.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 11.132ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_908.svg">
is an elementary propositional function. Hence by <a href="#_2_11" class="pginternal">*2·11</a>,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash : {\sim}{\phi} \lor {\sim}{\psi}p .\lor. {\sim}({\sim}{\phi}p \lor {\sim}{\psi}p)\text{.} \]" src="images/909.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.437ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_909.svg"></span></p>

<p>Hence by <a href="#_2_32" class="pginternal">*2·32</a> and <a href="#_1_01" class="pginternal">*1·01</a>,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash \colon\ldotp {\phi}p .\supset : {\psi}p .\supset. {\sim}({\sim}{\phi}p \lor {\sim}{\psi}p)\text{,} \]" src="images/910.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.569ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_910.svg"></span>
<i>i.e.</i> by <a href="#_3_01" class="pginternal">*3·01</a>,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash \colon\ldotp {\phi}p . \supset: {\psi}p .\supset. {\phi}p . {\psi}p\text{.} \]" src="images/911.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 23.02ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_911.svg"></span></p>

<p>Hence by <a href="#_1_11" class="pginternal">*1·11</a>, when we have "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash . {\phi}p\)" src="images/912.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.875ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_912.svg">" and "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash .{\psi}p\)" src="images/913.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.999ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_913.svg">"
we have "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash . {\phi}p . {\psi}p\)" src="images/914.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 8.492ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_914.svg">." This proposition
is <a href="#_3_03" class="pginternal">*3·03</a>. It is to be understood, like <a href="#_1_72" class="pginternal">*1·72</a>, as applying also to
functions of two or more variables.</p>

<p>The above is the practically most useful form of the axiom of
identification of real variables (cf. <a href="#_1_72" class="pginternal">*1·72</a>). In practice, when the
restriction to <i>elementary</i> propositions and propositional
functions has been removed, a convenient means by which two functions
can often be recognized as taking arguments of the same type is the
following:</p>

<p>If <img alt="" data-tex="\({\phi}x\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 2.643ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_51"> contains, in any way, a constituent <img alt="" data-tex="\(\chi(x, y, z,\ldots)\)" src="images/915.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.301ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_915.svg">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\({\psi}x\)" src="images/245.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 2.767ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_245.svg_2"> contains, in any way, a constituent <img alt="" data-tex="\(\chi(x, u, v, \ldots)\)" src="images/916.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.532ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_916.svg">,
then both <img alt="" data-tex="\({\phi}x\)" src="images/140.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 2.643ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_140.svg_52"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\({\psi}x\)" src="images/245.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 2.767ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_245.svg_3"> take arguments<span class="pagenum" id="Page_115">[Pg 115]</span>
of the type of the argument <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_310"> in <img alt="" data-tex="\(\chi(x, y, z, ...)\)" src="images/917.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.667ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_917.svg">, and
therefore both <img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi x\)" src="images/128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 2.643ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_128.svg_83"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\psi x\)" src="images/176.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 2.767ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_176.svg_20"> take arguments of the same
type. Hence, in such a case, if both <img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi x\)" src="images/128.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 2.643ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_128.svg_84"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\psi x\)" src="images/176.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 2.767ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_176.svg_21"> can be
asserted, so can <img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi x\ldotp \psi x\)" src="images/918.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.416ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_918.svg">.</p>

<p>As an example of the use of this proposition, take the proof of <a href="#_3_47" class="pginternal">*3·47</a>.
We there prove
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} &amp;\vdash \colon\ldotp p\supset r\ldotp q\supset s\ldotp\supset :p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset \ldotp q\ldotp r &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \text{and}\quad &amp;\vdash \colon\ldotp p\supset r\ldotp q\supset s\ldotp \supset :q\ldotp r\ldotp\supset \ldotp r\ldotp s &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \end{aligned} \]" src="images/919.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 47.222ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_919.svg"></span>
and what we wish to prove is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ p\supset r\ldotp q\supset s\ldotp\supset :p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset \ldotp r\ldotp s, \]" src="images/920.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.997ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_920.svg"></span>
which is <a href="#_3_47" class="pginternal">*3·47</a>. Now in (1) and (2), <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_212">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_140">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_28">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(s\)" src="images/40.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.061ex; height: 1.023ex;" id="img_images_40.svg_3"> are
elementary propositions (as everywhere in Section A); hence by *1·7·71,
applied repeatedly, "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\supset r\ldotp q\supset r\ldotp\supset:p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset \ldotp q\ldotp r\)" src="images/921.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.307ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_921.svg">"
and "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\supset r\ldotp q\supset s\ldotp\supset :q\ldotp r\ldotp\supset \ldotp r\ldotp s\)" src="images/922.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.251ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_922.svg">"
are elementary propositional functions. Hence by <a href="#_3_03" class="pginternal">*3·03</a>, we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash \colon\colon p\supset r\ldotp q\supset s\ldotp\supset :p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset \ldotp q\ldotp r \colon\ldotp  p\supset r\ldotp q\supset s\ldotp\supset :q\ldotp r\ldotp\supset \ldotp r\ldotp s, \]" src="images/923.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 56.634ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_923.svg"></span>
whence the result follows by <a href="#_3_43" class="pginternal">*3·43</a> and <a href="#_3_33" class="pginternal">*3·33</a>.</p>

<p>The principal propositions of the present number are the following:</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·2</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp p\ldotp\supset :q\ldotp\supset \ldotp p\ldotp q\)" src="images/924.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 16.554ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_924.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e</i>. "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_213"> implies that <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_141"> implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\ldotp q\)" src="images/925.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 3.185ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_925.svg">,"
<i>i.e</i>. if each of two propositions is true, so is their logical
product.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_3_26">*3·26</a></b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :p\ldotp q\ldotp \supset \ldotp p\)" src="images/926.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 10.735ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_926.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·27</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset \ldotp q\)" src="images/927.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 10.638ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_927.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e</i>. if the logical product of two propositions is true, then
each of the two propositions severally is true.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·3</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset \ldotp r:\supset :p\ldotp\supset \ldotp q\supset r\)" src="images/928.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.635ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_928.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e</i>. if <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_214"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_142"> jointly imply <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_29">, then <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_215"> implies
that <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_143"> implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_30">. This principle (following Peano) will be
called "exportation," because <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_144"> is "exported" from the hypothesis.
It will be referred to as "Exp."</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·31</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp p\ldotp\supset \ldotp q\supset r:\supset :p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset \ldotp r\)" src="images/929.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.635ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_929.svg"></p>

<p>This is the correlative of the above, and will be called (following
Peano) "importation" (referred to as "Imp").</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·35</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :p\ldotp p\supset q\ldotp\supset \ldotp q\)" src="images/930.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 14.793ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_930.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e</i>. "if <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_216"> is true, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_145"> follows from it, then <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_146"> is
true." This will be called the "principle of assertion" (referred to as
"Ass"). It differs from *1·1 by the fact that it does not apply only
when <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_217"> really is true, but requires merely the <i>hypothesis</i>
that p is true.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·43</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp p\supset q\ldotp p\supset r\ldotp\supset :p\ldotp\supset \ldotp q\ldotp r\)" src="images/931.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 26.773ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_931.svg"></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_116">[Pg 116]</span></p>

<p><i>I.e</i>. if a proposition implies each of two propositions, then it
implies their logical product. This is called by Peano the "principle
of composition." It will be referred to as "Comp."</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·45.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp  p \,\supset:\, q \,\supset.\, p \,.\, r \,\supset\, q \,.\, r\)" src="images/932.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.641ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_932.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> both sides of an implication may be multiplied by a common
factor. This is called by Peano the "principle of the factor." It will
be referred to as "Fact."</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·47.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p \supset r . q \supset s.  \supset: p . q. \supset. r . s\)" src="images/933.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 28.763ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_933.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_218"> implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_147"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_31"> implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(s\)" src="images/40.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.061ex; height: 1.023ex;" id="img_images_40.svg_4">, then
<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_219"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_148"> jointly imply <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_32"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(s\)" src="images/40.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.023ex; width: 1.061ex; height: 1.023ex;" id="img_images_40.svg_5"> jointly. The law of
contradiction, "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.{\sim}(p.{\sim}p\)" src="images/934.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.071ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_934.svg">)," is proved in this number
(<a href="#_3_24" class="pginternal">*3·24</a>); but in spite of its fame we have found few occasions for its
use.</p>

<hr class="tb">

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(p . q . = {\sim} ({\sim} p \lor {\sim} q) \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/935.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 22.997ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_935.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\supset q\supset r.=.p\supset q.q \supset r \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/936.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 28.969ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_936.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_3_03">*3·03</a>.</b> Given two asserted elementary propositional functions
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\phi p\)" src="images/937.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.875ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_937.svg">" and "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\psi p\)" src="images/938.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.999ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_938.svg">" whose arguments are
elementary propositions, we have <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\phi p.\psi p\)" src="images/939.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 8.492ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_939.svg">.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .\text{*1·7·72.*2·11} . \supset \vdash : {\sim} \psi p \lor {\sim} \psi p . \lor . {\sim}({\sim} \psi p \lor {\sim} \psi p) &amp;\qquad \text{(1)} \\ \vdash .\text{(1).*2·32.(*1·01)} . \supset \vdash \vdash \psi p . \supset : \psi p . \supset . {\sim} ({\sim} \psi p \lor {\sim} \psi p) &amp;\qquad \text{(2)} \\ \vdash .\text{(2).(*3·03)} . \supset \vdash \vdash \psi p . \supset : \psi p . \supset . \psi p . \psi p &amp;\qquad \text{(3)} \\ \vdash .\text{(3).*1·11} . \supset \vdash . \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/940.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 62.238ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_940.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·1.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : p . q . \supset . {\sim} ({\sim} p \lor {\sim} q) \quad [\text{Id. (*3·01)}]\)" src="images/941.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.034ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_941.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·11.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : {\sim} ({\sim} p \lor {\sim} q) . \supset . p . q \quad [\text{Id.} (*3·01)]\)" src="images/942.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.474ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_942.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·12.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : {\sim} p . \lor . {\sim} q . \lor . p . q \quad \left[\text{*2·11} \frac{{\sim} p \lor {\sim} q}{p}\right]\)" src="images/943.svg" style="vertical-align: -1.469ex; width: 34.587ex; height: 4.07ex;" id="img_images_943.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·13.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : {\sim} (p . q) . \supset . {\sim} p \lor {\sim} q \quad [\text{*3·11.Transp}]\)" src="images/944.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 37.693ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_944.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·14.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : {\sim} p \lor {\sim} q . \supset . {\sim} (p . q) \quad [\text{*3·1.Transp}]\)" src="images/945.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 36.562ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_945.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p . \supset : q . \supset . p . q \quad [\text{*3·12}] \)" src="images/946.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 25.228ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_946.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·21.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp q . \supset : p . \supset . p . q \quad [\text{*3·2.Comm}]\)" src="images/947.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.26ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_947.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·22.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : p . q . \supset . q . p\)" src="images/948.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 12.782ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_948.svg"></p>

<p>This is one form of the commutative law for logical multiplication. A
more complete form is given in <a href="#_4_3" class="pginternal">*4·3</a>.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} [\text{*3·13} \frac{q,p}{p,q}] \vdash : \sim (q . p) . &amp;\supset . \sim q \lor \sim p. \\ [\text{Perm}] &amp;\supset . \sim p \lor \sim q. \\ [\text{*3·14}] &amp;\supset . \sim (p . q) &amp;\qquad \text{(1)} \\ \vdash . \text{(1) . Transp}. \supset \vdash . \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/949.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.624ex; width: 48.5ex; height: 12.38ex;" id="img_images_949.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_117">[Pg 117]</span></p>

<p>Note that, in the above proof, "(1)" stands for the proposition
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \unicode{x201c}\sim (q\ldotp p)\ldotp\supset\ldotp\sim (p\ldotp q),\unicode{x201d} \]" src="images/950.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 22.336ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_950.svg"></span>
as was explained in the proof of <a href="#_2_31" class="pginternal">*2·31</a>.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_3_24">*3·24</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\ldotp\sim (p\ldotp\sim p)\)" src="images/951.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.208ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_951.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{align*} \left [\text{*2·11}\, \frac{\sim p}{p}\right]  &amp;\vdash\ldotp \sim p\lor\sim (\sim p)\ldotp \supset\\ \left [\text{*3·14}\, \frac{\sim p}{q}\right]  &amp;\vdash\ldotp\sim (p\ldotp\sim p)\\ \end{align*} \]" src="images/952.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.201ex; width: 31.566ex; height: 11.534ex;" id="img_images_952.svg"></span></p>

<p>The above is the law of contradiction.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·26.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset\ldotp p\)" src="images/953.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 10.483ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_953.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \left[\text{*2·02}\, \frac{q,\,p}{p,\,q}\right] &amp;\vdash\colon p\ldotp\supset\ldotp  q\supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ [\text{(1).*1·01})] &amp;\vdash\colon\sim p\ldotp \lor\ldotp \sim q\lor p\colon\\ [\text{*2·31}] \supset&amp;\vdash\colon \sim p\lor\sim q\ldotp\lor\ldotp p\colon\\ \left [\text{*2·53} \frac{\sim p\lor\sim q,\,p}{p,\,q}\right] \supset &amp;\vdash \colon\sim (\sim p\lor\sim q)\ldotp \supset\ldotp p &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ [\text{(2).*3·01)}] &amp;\vdash\colon p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset\ldotp p \end{array} \]" src="images/954.svg" style="vertical-align: -8.708ex; width: 49.88ex; height: 18.548ex;" id="img_images_954.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·27.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon p\ldotp q\ldotp\supset\ldotp q\)" src="images/955.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 10.386ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_955.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} [\text{*3·22}] \vdash\colon p\ldotp q\ldotp&amp;\supset\ldotp q\ldotp p\ldotp \\ \left[\text{*3·26} \frac{q,\,p}{p,\,q} \right] &amp; \supset\ldotp q\colon\supset\vdash\ldotp \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/956.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.053ex; width: 29.283ex; height: 7.238ex;" id="img_images_956.svg"></span></p>

<p>*3·26·27 will both be called the "principle of simplification," like
<a href="#_2_02" class="pginternal">*2·02</a>, from which they are deduced. They will be referred to as "Simp."</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·3.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\ldotp q\ldotp \supset \ldotp r\colon \supset \colon p\ldotp \supset \ldotp q \supset r\)" src="images/957.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.132ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_957.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} [\text{Id.}(\text{*3·01})] \vdash\colon\ldotp p\ldotp q\ldotp \supset \ldotp r\colon &amp;\supset \colon\sim (\sim p \lor \sim q)\ldotp \supset \ldotp r\colon\\ [\text{Transp}] &amp;\supset\colon\sim r\ldotp \supset\ldotp\sim p\ lor \sim q\colon\\ [\text{Id.}(\text{*1·01})] &amp;\supset\colon\sim r\ldotp \supset \ldotp p \supset \sim q\colon\\ [\text{Comm}] &amp;\supset\colon p\ldotp \supset \ldotp \sim r\supset \sim q\colon\\ [\text{Transp.Syll}] &amp;\supset\colon p\ldotp \supset \ldotp q\supset r\colon\ldotp \supset\vdash\ldotp \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/958.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.9ex; width: 49.499ex; height: 14.932ex;" id="img_images_958.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·31.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\ldotp \supset \ldotp q \supset r\colon \supset \colon p\ldotp q\ldotp \supset\ldotp r\)" src="images/959.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.132ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_959.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} [\text{Id.}(\text{*1·01})] \vdash\colon\ldotp p\ldotp \supset \ldotp q \supset r\colon &amp;\supset \colon \sim p\ldotp \lor \ldotp \sim q\lor r\colon\\ [\text{*2·31}] &amp;\supset\colon\sim p\lor\sim q\ldotp \lor \ldotp r\colon\\ \left[\text{*2·53}\, \frac{\sim p\lor \sim q,\,r}{p,\,q}\right] &amp;\supset \colon\sim (\sim p\lor \sim q)\ldotp \supset \ldotp r\colon\\ [\text{Id.(*3·01)}] &amp;\supset \colon p\ldotp q\ldotp \supset\ldotp r\colon\ldotp \supset\vdash\ldotp \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/960.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.221ex; width: 49.499ex; height: 13.572ex;" id="img_images_960.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_118">[Pg 118]</span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_3_33">*3·33</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash :p\supset q .q\supset r. \supset .p\supset r \quad[\text{Syll. Imp}]\)" src="images/961.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.252ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_961.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·34.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:q\supset r.p\supset q.\supset.p\supset r \quad[\text{Syll. Imp}]\)" src="images/962.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.252ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_962.svg"></p>

<p>These two propositions will hereafter be referred to as "Syll"; they
are usually more convenient than either <a href="#_2_05" class="pginternal">*2·05</a> or <a href="#_2_06" class="pginternal">*2·06</a>.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·35.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : p. p \supset q . \supset . q \quad[\text{*2·27. Imp}]\)" src="images/963.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 28.621ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_963.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·37.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp  p . q . \supset . r :\supset: p. {\sim} r. \supset . {\sim} q\)" src="images/964.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 27.145ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_964.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash . \text{Transp} . &amp;\supset \vdash : q\supset r . \supset . {\sim}r \supset {\sim}q:\\ [\text{Syll}] &amp;\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp  p.\supset.q\supset r:\supset:p.\supset.{\sim}r\supset{\sim}q &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash . \text{Exp}. &amp;\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp  p . q . \supset . r :\supset: p .\supset. q\supset r &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash . \text{Imp}. &amp;\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp p.\supset.{\sim}r\supset{\sim}q :\supset: p.{\sim}r .\supset. {\sim}q &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \vdash . \text{(2).(1).(3).Syll}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/965.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.9ex; width: 73.009ex; height: 14.932ex;" id="img_images_965.svg"></span></p>

<p>This is another form of transposition.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·4.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p.q.\supset.p\supset q \quad[\text{*2·51.Transp.(*1·01. *3·01)}]\)" src="images/966.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 45.046ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_966.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·41.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp  p \supset r . \supset : p . q . \supset . r \quad[\text{*3·26.Syll}]\)" src="images/967.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.584ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_967.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·42.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp  q \supset r . \supset : p . q . \supset . r \quad[\text{*3·27.Syll}]\)" src="images/968.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.487ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_968.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_3_43">*3·43</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.p\supset r. \supset : p . \supset . q . r\)" src="images/969.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 26.773ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_969.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash . \text{*3·2}.\supset \vdash \colon\ldotp  q . \supset : r . \supset . q . r &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash . \text{(1). Syll}. \supset \vdash \colon\colon  p \supset q . &amp;\supset \colon\ldotp  p . \supset : r. \supset . q . r\colon\ldotp \\ [\text{*2·77}] &amp;\supset \colon\ldotp  p \supset r . \supset : p . \supset . q . r &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash . \text{(2). Imp}. \supset \vdash . \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/970.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 58.386ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_970.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_3_44">*3·44</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp  q \supset p . r \supset p . \supset : q \lor r . \supset . p\)" src="images/971.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 28.281ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_971.svg"></p>

<p>This principle is analogous to <a href="#_3_43" class="pginternal">*3·43</a>. The analogy between *3·43 and
<a href="#_3_44" class="pginternal">*3·44</a> is of a sort which generally subsists between formulae concerning
products and formulae concerning sums.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash . \text{Syll}. \supset \vdash\colon\ldotp  {\sim}q\supset r . r\supset p . &amp;\supset:{\sim}q\supset p:\\ [\text{*2·6}] &amp;\supset :q\supset p . \supset . p &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash .\text{(1).Exp}. \supset \vdash\colon\colon  {\sim}q \supset r . &amp;\supset\colon\ldotp  r\supset p .\supset: q\supset p . \supset . p\colon\ldotp\\ [\text{Comm.Imp}] &amp;\supset\colon\ldotp q \supset p . r\supset p . \supset . p &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(2).Comm}. &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp  q \supset p . r \supset p. \supset: {\sim}q \supset r .\supset. p\colon\ldotp \\ [\text{*2·53.Syll}] &amp;\supset \vdash . \text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/972.svg" style="vertical-align: -8.484ex; width: 71.789ex; height: 18.1ex;" id="img_images_972.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_119">[Pg 119]</span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·45.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\supset :p.r.\supset .q.r\)" src="images/973.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 22.618ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_973.svg"></p>

<p>This principle shows that we may multiply both sides of an implication
by a common factor; hence it is called by Peano the "principle of
the factor." We shall refer to it as "Fact." It is the analogue, for
multiplication, of the primitive proposition <a href="#_1_6" class="pginternal">*1·6</a>.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{Syll}\, \frac{{\sim}r}{r} .\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.&amp;\supset :q\supset {\sim}r.\supset .p\supset {\sim}r:\\ [\text{Transp}] &amp;\supset :{\sim}(p\supset {\sim}r).\supset .{\sim}(q\supset {\sim}r)\colon\ldotp \\ [\text{Id.(*1·01.*3·01)}] \supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/974.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.849ex; width: 57.754ex; height: 8.83ex;" id="img_images_974.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_3_47">*3·47</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset r.q\supset s.\supset :p.q.\supset .r.s\)" src="images/975.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 28.763ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_975.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition, or rather its analogue for classes, was proved by
Leibniz, and evidently pleased him, since he calls it "præclarum
theorema<a class="fnanchor pginternal" href="#Footnote_48" id="FNanchor_48">[48]</a>."</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*3·26}.\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset r.q\supset s.&amp;\supset :p\supset r:\\ [\text{Fact}] &amp;\supset :p.q.\supset .r.q:\\ [\text{*3·22}] &amp;\supset :p.q.\supset .q.r &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash. \text{*3·27}.\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset r.q\supset s.&amp;\supset :q\supset s:\\ [\text{Fact}] &amp;\supset :q.r.\supset .s.r:\\ [\text{*3·22}] &amp;\supset :q.r.\supset .r.s &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).(2).*3·03.*2·83}.\supset \\ \qquad\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset r.q\supset s.\supset :p.q.\supset .r.s\colon\ldotp \supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/976.svg" style="vertical-align: -11.652ex; width: 70.506ex; height: 24.434ex;" id="img_images_976.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*3·48.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset r.q\supset s.\supset :p\lor q.\supset .r\lor s\)" src="images/977.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 31.78ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_977.svg"></p>

<p>This theorem is the analogue of <a href="#_3_47" class="pginternal">*3·47</a>.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*3·26}.\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset r.q\supset s.&amp;\supset :p\supset r:\\ [\text{Sum}] &amp;\supset :p\lor q.\supset .r\lor q:\\ [\text{Perm}] &amp;\supset :p\lor q.\supset .q\lor r &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{*3·27}.\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset r.q\supset s.&amp;\supset :q\supset s:\\ [\text{Sum}] &amp;\supset :q\lor r.\supset .s\lor r:\\ [\text{Perm}] &amp;\supset :q\lor r.\supset .r\lor s &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).(2).*2·83}.\supset \\ \qquad\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset r.q\supset s.\supset :p\lor q.\supset .r\lor s\colon\ldotp \supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/978.svg" style="vertical-align: -11.652ex; width: 76.54ex; height: 24.434ex;" id="img_images_978.svg"></span></p>
