<hr class="chap x-ebookmaker-drop">

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_120">[Pg 120]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_4">*4. EQUIVALENCE AND FORMAL RULES.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *4.</p>

<p>In this number, we shall be concerned with rules analogous, more or
less, to those of ordinary algebra. It is from these rules that the
usual "calculus of formal logic" starts. Treated as a "calculus," the
rules of deduction are capable of many other interpretations. But all
other interpretations depend upon the one here considered, since in all
of them we deduce consequences from our rules, and thus presuppose the
theory of deduction. One very simple interpretation of the "calculus"
is as follows: The entities considered are to be numbers which are all
either <img alt="" data-tex="\(0\)" src="images/979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.557ex;" id="img_images_979.svg"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\)" src="images/395.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.507ex;" id="img_images_395.svg_3">; "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p \supset q\)" src="images/71.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.196ex; height: 1.661ex;" id="img_images_71.svg_10">" is to have the value <img alt="" data-tex="\(0\)" src="images/979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.557ex;" id="img_images_979.svg_1">
if <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_220"> is <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\)" src="images/395.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.507ex;" id="img_images_395.svg_4"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_149"> is <img alt="" data-tex="\(0\)" src="images/979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.557ex;" id="img_images_979.svg_2">; otherwise it is to have the
value <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\)" src="images/395.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.507ex;" id="img_images_395.svg_5">; <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}p\)" src="images/58.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.898ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_58.svg_5"> is to be <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\)" src="images/395.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.507ex;" id="img_images_395.svg_6"> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_221"> is <img alt="" data-tex="\(0\)" src="images/979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.557ex;" id="img_images_979.svg_3">, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(0\)" src="images/979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.557ex;" id="img_images_979.svg_4">
if <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_222"> is <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\)" src="images/395.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.507ex;" id="img_images_395.svg_7">; <img alt="" data-tex="\(p . q\)" src="images/75.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 3.185ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_75.svg_5"> is to be <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\)" src="images/395.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.507ex;" id="img_images_395.svg_8"> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_223"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_150"> are
both <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\)" src="images/395.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.507ex;" id="img_images_395.svg_9">, and is to be <img alt="" data-tex="\(0\)" src="images/979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.557ex;" id="img_images_979.svg_5"> in any other case; <img alt="" data-tex="\(p \lor q\)" src="images/59.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 4.693ex; height: 1.792ex;" id="img_images_59.svg_7"> is to
be <img alt="" data-tex="\(0\)" src="images/979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.557ex;" id="img_images_979.svg_6"> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_224"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_151"> are both <img alt="" data-tex="\(0\)" src="images/979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.557ex;" id="img_images_979.svg_7">, and is to be <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\)" src="images/395.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.507ex;" id="img_images_395.svg_10"> in any
other case; and the assertion-sign is to mean that what follows has the
value <img alt="" data-tex="\(1\)" src="images/395.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.131ex; height: 1.507ex;" id="img_images_395.svg_11">. Symbolic logic considered as a calculus has undoubtedly
much interest on its own account; but in our opinion this aspect has
hitherto been too much emphasized, at the expense of the aspect in
which symbolic logic is merely the most elementary part of mathematics,
and the logical prerequisite of all the rest. For this reason, we shall
only deal briefly with what is required for the algebra of symbolic
logic.</p>

<p>When each of two propositions implies the other, we say that the two
are <i>equivalent</i>, which we write "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p \equiv q\)" src="images/73.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.196ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_73.svg_6">." We put</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(p \equiv q .=. p \supset q . q \supset p \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/980.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.049ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_980.svg"></p>

<p>It is obvious that two propositions are equivalent when, and only when,
both are true or both are false. Following Frege, we shall call the
<i>truth-value of a proposition</i> truth if it is true, and falsehood
if it is false. Thus two propositions are equivalent when they have the
same truth-value.</p>

<p>It should be observed that, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(p \equiv q\)" src="images/73.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 5.196ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_73.svg_7">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_152"> may be substituted
for <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_225"> without altering the truth-value of any function of <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_226">
which involves no primitive ideas except those enumerated in <a href="#_1" class="pginternal">*1</a>. This
can be proved in each separate case, but not generally, because we have
no means of specifying (with our apparatus of primitive ideas) that a
function is one which can be built up out<span class="pagenum" id="Page_121">[Pg 121]</span> of these ideas alone. We
shall give the name of a <i>truth-function</i> to a function <img alt="" data-tex="\(f(p)\)" src="images/76.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 4.143ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_76.svg_4">
whose argument is a proposition, and whose truth-value depends only
upon the truth-value of its argument. All the functions of propositions
with which we shall be specially concerned will be truth-functions,
<i>i.e.</i> we shall have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ p\equiv q.\supset.f(p)\equiv f(q). \]" src="images/981.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 20.802ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_981.svg"></span>
The reason of this is, that the functions of propositions with which
we deal are all built up by means of the primitive ideas of <a href="#_1" class="pginternal">*1</a>. But it
is not a universal characteristic of functions of propositions to be
truth-functions. For example, "<img alt="" data-tex="\(A\)" src="images/38.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.697ex; height: 1.62ex;" id="img_images_38.svg_26"> believes <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_227">" may be true for
one true value of <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_228"> and false for another.</p>

<p>The principal propositions of this number are the following:</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·1.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p\supset q.\equiv.{\sim} q\supset{\sim} p\)" src="images/982.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 20.324ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_982.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·11.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p\equiv q.\equiv.{\sim} p\equiv{\sim} q\)" src="images/983.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 20.324ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_983.svg"></p>

<p>These are both forms of the "principle of transposition."</p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_4_13">*4·13</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.p\equiv{\sim}({\sim} p)\)" src="images/984.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 12.962ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_984.svg"></p>

<p>This is the principle of double negation, <i>i.e.</i> a proposition is
equivalent to the falsehood of its negation.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.p\equiv p\)" src="images/985.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 7.681ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_985.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·21.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p\equiv q.\equiv.q\equiv p\)" src="images/986.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 16.804ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_986.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·22.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p\equiv q.q\equiv r.\supset.p\equiv r\)" src="images/987.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 22.868ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_987.svg"></p>

<p>These propositions assert that equivalence is <i>reflexive</i>,
<i>symmetrical</i> and <i>transitive</i>.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_4_24">*4·24</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p.\equiv.p.p\)" src="images/988.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 10.832ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_988.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·25.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p.\equiv.p\lor p\)" src="images/989.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 12.341ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_989.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_229"> is equivalent to "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_230"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_231">" and to "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_232"> or
<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_233">," which are two forms of the <i>law of tautology</i>, and are the
source of the principal differences between the algebra of symbolic
logic and ordinary algebra.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_4_3">*4·3</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p.q.\equiv.q.p\)" src="images/990.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 12.782ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_990.svg"></p>

<p>This is the commutative law for the product of propositions.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·31.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p\lor q.\equiv.q\lor p\)" src="images/991.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 15.799ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_991.svg"></p>

<p>This is the commutative law for the sum of propositions.</p>

<p>The associative laws for multiplication and addition of propositions,
namely</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·32.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:(p.q).r.\equiv.p.(q.r)\)" src="images/992.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 20.355ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_992.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·33.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:(p\lor q)\lor r.\equiv.p\lor (q\lor r)\)" src="images/993.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.389ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_993.svg"></p>

<p>The distributive law in the two forms</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_122">[Pg 122]</span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·4.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p.q\lor r.\equiv:p.q.\lor.p.r\)" src="images/994.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 24.008ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_994.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·41.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p.\lor.q.r:\equiv.p\lor q.p\lor r\)" src="images/995.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 25.517ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_995.svg"></p>

<p>The second of these forms has no analogue in ordinary algebra.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·71.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\equiv:p.\equiv.p.q\)" src="images/996.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 20.709ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_996.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_234"> implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_153"> when, and only when, <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_235"> is
equivalent to <img alt="" data-tex="\(p.q\)" src="images/997.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 3.185ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_997.svg">. This proposition is used constantly; it enables
us to replace any implication by an equivalence.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·73.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp q.\supset:p.\equiv.p.q\)" src="images/998.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 16.554ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_998.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> a true factor may be dropped from or added to a proposition
without altering the truth-value of the proposition.</p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash .\text{*3·26.} &amp;\supset \vdash : p \equiv q . q \equiv r . \supset . p \equiv q \\ [\text{*3·26}] &amp;\supset . p \supset q &amp;\qquad \text{(1)} \\ \vdash .\text{*3·27}. &amp;\supset \vdash : p \equiv q . q \equiv r . \supset . q \equiv r \\ [\text{*3·26}] &amp;\supset . q \supset r &amp;\qquad \text{(2)} \\ \vdash . \text{(1) . (2) .*2·83}. &amp;\supset \vdash : p \equiv q . q \equiv r . \supset . p \supset r &amp;\qquad \text{(3)} \\ \vdash .\text{*3·27}. &amp;\supset \vdash : p \equiv q . q \equiv r . \supset . q \equiv r \\ [\text{*3·27}] &amp;\supset . r \supset q &amp;\qquad \text{(4)} \\ \vdash .\text{*3·26}. &amp;\supset \vdash : p \equiv q . q \equiv r . \supset . p \equiv q \\ [\text{*3·27}] &amp;\supset . q \supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(5)} \\ \vdash . \text{(4) . (5) .*2·83}. &amp;\supset \vdash : p \equiv q . q \equiv r . \supset . r \supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(6)} \\ \vdash . \text{(3) . (6) . <p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_123">[Pg 123]</span></p>

<p><i>Note.</i> The above three propositions show that the relation of
equivalence is reflexive (<a href="#_4_2" class="pginternal">*4·2</a>), symmetrical (<a href="#_4_21" class="pginternal">*4·21</a>), and transitive
(<a href="#_4_22" class="pginternal">*4·22</a>). Implication is reflexive and transitive, but not symmetrical.
The properties of being symmetrical, transitive, and (at least within a
certain field) reflexive are essential to any relation which is to have
the formal characters of equality.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·24.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p.\equiv.p.p\)" src="images/988.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 10.832ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_988.svg_1"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} &amp;\vdash.\text{*3·26}.&amp;\supset\vdash:p.p.\supset.p &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ &amp;\vdash.\text{*3·2}.&amp;\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp p.\supset:p.\supset.p.p.:\\ &amp;[\text{*2·43}] &amp;\supset\vdash:p.\supset.p.p &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ &amp;\vdash.\text{(1).(2).*3·2}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1010.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 57.77ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_1010.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>Note.</i> *4·24·25 are two forms of the <i>law of tautology</i>,
which is what chiefly distinguishes the algebra of symbolic logic from
ordinary algebra.</p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \phi(p,q).\supset.\phi(q,p), \]" src="images/1013.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.988ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1013.svg"></span>
we have also
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \phi(p,q).\equiv.\phi(q,p). \]" src="images/1014.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.988ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1014.svg"></span>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*4·15}. \supset\vdash\colon\ldotp p.q.\supset.{\sim}r:&amp;\equiv:q.r.\supset.{\sim}p:\\ [\text{*4·12}] &amp;\equiv:p.\supset.{\sim}(q.r) &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*4·11}.\supset\vdash:{\sim}(p.q.\supset.{\sim}r).&amp;\equiv.{\sim}{p.\supset.{\sim}(q.r)}:\\ [\text{(*1·01.*3·01)}]\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1017.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 59.578ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_1017.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*2·2}. &amp;\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp p.\supset:p.\lor.p.q &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{Id.*3·26}. &amp;\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset p:p.q.\supset.p\colon\ldotp \\ [\text{*3·44}] &amp;\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp p.\lor.p.q:\supset.p &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).(2)}. &amp;\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1036.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 44.88ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_1036.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·45.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p.\equiv .p.p\lor q \quad[\text{*3·26.*2·2}]\)" src="images/1037.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.713ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1037.svg"></p>

<p>The following formulae are due to De Morgan, or rather, are the
propositional analogues of formulae given by De Morgan for classes. The
first of them, it will be observed, merely embodies our definition of
the logical product.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·5.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: p.q.\equiv .{\sim}({\sim}p\lor{\sim}q) \quad[\text{*4·2. (*3·01)}]\)" src="images/1038.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 36.982ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1038.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">

<p class="nind">

<b>*4·55.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: {\sim}({\sim}p.q).\equiv .p\lor{\sim}q \quad[\text{*4·54·12}]\)" src="images/1043.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 32.896ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1043.svg"></p>

<b>*4·56.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: {\sim}p.{\sim}q.\equiv .{\sim}(p\lor q) \quad\left[\text{*4·54} \frac{{\sim}q}{q}.\text{*4·13}\right]\)" src="images/1044.svg" style="vertical-align: -1.469ex; width: 40.396ex; height: 4.07ex;" id="img_images_1044.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·57.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: {\sim}({\sim}p.{\sim}q).\equiv .p\lor q \quad[\text{*4·56·12}]\)" src="images/1045.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 32.896ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1045.svg"></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_126">[Pg 126]</span></p>

<p>The following formulae are obtained immediately from the above. They
are important as showing how to transform implications into sums or
into denials of products, and vice versa. It will be observed that the
first of them merely embodies the definition <a href="#_1_01" class="pginternal">*1·01</a>.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·6.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: p\supset q.\equiv.{\sim}p\lor q \quad[\text{*4·2.(*1·01)}]\)" src="images/1046.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.147ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1046.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·61.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: {\sim}(p\supset q).\equiv.p.{\sim}q \quad[\text{*4·6·11·52}]\)" src="images/1047.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.399ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1047.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·62.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: p\supset {\sim}q.\equiv.{\sim}p\lor {\sim}q \quad\left[\text{*4·6}\, \frac{{\sim}q}{q}\right]\)" src="images/1048.svg" style="vertical-align: -1.469ex; width: 33.733ex; height: 4.07ex;" id="img_images_1048.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_4_63">*4·63</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: {\sim}(p\supset {\sim}q).\equiv.p.q \quad[\text{*4·62·11·5}]\)" src="images/1049.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 33.399ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1049.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·67.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:{\sim}({\sim}p\supset {\sim}q).\equiv.{\sim}p.q \quad[\text{*4·66·11·54}]\)" src="images/1053.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 38.051ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1053.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·7.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\equiv:p.\supset .p.q\)" src="images/1054.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 20.709ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_1054.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin {array}{l} \vdash.\text{*3·27.Syll}. &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p.\supset .p.q:\supset .p\supset q &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{Comp} &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset p.p\supset q.\supset :p.\supset .p.q\colon\ldotp \\ [\text{Exp}] &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\colon p\supset p.\supset \colon\ldotp p\supset q.\supset :p.\supset .p.q\colon\colon \\ [\text{Id}] &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\supset :p.\supset .p.q &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).(2)}. &amp;\supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1055.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.9ex; width: 58.627ex; height: 14.932ex;" id="img_images_1055.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·71.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\equiv:p.\equiv.p.q\)" src="images/996.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 20.709ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_996.svg_1"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin {array}{l} \vdash.\text{*3·21}. &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\colon p.q.\supset .p:\supset \colon\ldotp p.\supset .p.q:\supset :p.\equiv.p.q\colon\colon\\ [\text{*3·26}] &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p.\supset .p.q:\supset :p.\equiv.p.q &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{*3·26}. &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p.\equiv.p.q:\supset :p.\supset .p.q &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).(2)}. &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p.\supset .p.q:\equiv:p.\equiv.p.q &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \vdash.\text{(3).*4·7·22}.&amp;\supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1056.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.9ex; width: 65.772ex; height: 14.932ex;" id="img_images_1056.svg"></span></p>

<p>The above proposition is constantly used. It enables us to transform
every implication into an equivalence, which is an advantage if we
wish to assimilate symbolic logic as far as possible to ordinary
algebra. But when symbolic logic is regarded as an instrument of proof,
we need implications, and it is usually inconvenient to substitute
equivalences. Similar remarks apply to the following proposition.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·72.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\equiv:q.\equiv.p\lor q\)" src="images/1057.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 22.12ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_1057.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin {array}{l} \vdash.\text{*4·1}.\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.&amp;\equiv:{\sim}q\supset {\sim}p:\\ \left[\text{*4·71}\, \frac{{\sim}q,\,{\sim}p}{p,\,q}\right] &amp;\equiv:{\sim}q.\equiv.{\sim}q.{\sim}p:\\ [\text{*4·12}] &amp;\equiv:q.\equiv.{\sim}({\sim}q.{\sim}p):\\ [\text{*4·57}] &amp;\equiv:q.\equiv.q\lor p:\\ [\text{*4·31}] &amp;\equiv:q.\equiv.p\lor q\colon\ldotp \supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1058.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.804ex; width: 44.16ex; height: 16.74ex;" id="img_images_1058.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_127">[Pg 127]</span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·73.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp q.\supset :p.\equiv.p.q \quad[\text{Simp.*4·71}]\)" src="images/1059.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 30.886ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1059.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition is very useful, since it shows that a true factor may
be omitted from a product without altering its truth or falsehood, just
as a true hypothesis may be omitted from an implication.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·74.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp {\sim}p.\supset :q.\equiv.p\lor q \quad[\text{*2·21.*4·72}]\)" src="images/1060.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 34.28ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1060.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·76.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.p\supset r.\equiv:p.\supset .q.r \quad\left[\text{*4·41}\, \frac{{\sim}p}{p}.\text{(*1·01)}\right]\)" src="images/1061.svg" style="vertical-align: -1.469ex; width: 48.045ex; height: 4.07ex;" id="img_images_1061.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_4_77">*4·77</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp q\supset p.r\supset p.\equiv:q\lor r.\supset .p \quad[\text{*3·44. Add. *2·2}]\)" src="images/1062.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 47.58ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1062.svg"></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_4_78">*4·78</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\lor .p\supset r:\equiv:p.\supset .q\lor r\)" src="images/1063.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 31.048ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_1063.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin {array}{l} \vdash.\text{*4·2.(*1·01)}.\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp p\supset q.\lor .p\supset r:&amp;\equiv:{\sim}p\lor q.\lor .{\sim}p\lor r:\\ [\text{*4·33}] &amp;\equiv.{\sim}p.\lor .q\lor {\sim}p\lor r:\\ [\text{*4·31·37}] &amp;\equiv:{\sim}p.\lor .{\sim}p\lor q\lor r:\\ [\text{*4·33}] &amp;\equiv:{\sim}p\lor {\sim}p.\lor .q\lor r:\\ [\text{*4·25·37}] &amp;\equiv:{\sim}p.\lor .q\lor r:\\ [\text{*4·2.(*1·01)}] &amp;\equiv:p.\supset .q\lor r\colon\ldotp \supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1064.svg" style="vertical-align: -8.484ex; width: 61.008ex; height: 18.1ex;" id="img_images_1064.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind">
<b><a id="_4_79">*4·79</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp q\supset p.\lor .r\supset p:\equiv:q.r.\supset .p\)" src="images/1065.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 29.539ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_1065.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin {array}{l} \vdash.\text{*4·1·39}.\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp q\supset p.\lor .r\supset p:&amp;\equiv:{\sim}p\supset {\sim}q.\lor .{\sim}p\supset {\sim}r:\\ [\text{*4·78}] &amp;\equiv:{\sim}p.\supset .{\sim}q\lor {\sim}r:\\ [\text{*2·15}] &amp;\equiv:{\sim}({\sim}q\lor {\sim}r).\supset .p:\\ [\text{*4·2.(*3·01)}] &amp;\equiv:q.r.\supset .p\colon\ldotp \supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1066.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 58.083ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_1066.svg"></span></p>

<p><i>Note.</i> The analogues, for classes, of *4·78·79 are false. Take,
<i>e.g.</i> <a href="#_4_78" class="pginternal">*4·78</a>, and put <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_237"> = English people, <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_155"> = men, <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_33"> =
women. Then <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_238"> is contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_156"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_34">, but is not contained
in <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_157"> and is not contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_35">.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*4·8.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:p\supset {\sim}p.\equiv.{\sim}p \quad[\text{*2·01. Simp}]\)" src="images/1067.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.262ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_1067.svg"></p>

<hr class="chap x-ebookmaker-drop">

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_128">[Pg 128]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_5">*5. MISCELLANEOUS PROPOSITIONS.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *5.</p>

<p>The present number consists chiefly of propositions of two sorts:
(1) those which will be required as lemmas in one or more subsequent
proofs, (2) those which are on their own account illustrative, or would
be important in other developments than those that we wish to make.
A few of the propositions of this number, however, will be used very
frequently. These are:</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*5·1.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : p . q .\supset. p \equiv q\)" src="images/1075.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 14.793ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_1075.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> two propositions are equivalent if they are both true. (The
statement that two propositions are equivalent if they are both false
is <a href="#_5_21" class="pginternal">*5·21</a>.)</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*5·32.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp p .\supset. q \equiv r :\equiv: p . q .\equiv. p.r\)" src="images/1076.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 27.779ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_1076.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> to say that, on the hypothesis <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_239">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_158"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_36"> are
equivalent, is equivalent to saying that the joint assertion of <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_240">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_159"> is equivalent to the joint assertion of <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_241"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_37">. This
is a very useful rule in inference.</p>

<p class="nind">
<b>*5·6.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash \colon\ldotp p . {\sim}q .\supset. r :\equiv: p.\supset.q \lor r\)" src="images/1077.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 26.893ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_1077.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_242"> and not-<img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_160"> imply <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_38">" is equivalent to "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_243">
implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_161"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_39">."</p>

<p>Among propositions never subsequently referred to, but inserted for
their intrinsic interest, are the following: *5·11·12·13·14, which
state that, given any two propositions <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_244">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_162">, either <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_245"> or
<img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}p\)" src="images/58.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 2.898ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_58.svg_6"> must imply <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_163">, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_246"> must imply either <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_164"> or
not-<img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_165">, and either <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_247"> implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_166"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_167"> implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_248">; and
given any third proposition <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_40">, either <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_249"> implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_168"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_169">
implies <img alt="" data-tex="\(r\)" src="images/33.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.02ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_33.svg_41"><a class="fnanchor pginternal" href="#Footnote_49" id="FNanchor_49">[49]</a>.</p>

<p>Other propositions not subsequently referred to are *5·22·23·24; in
these it is shown that two propositions are not equivalent when, and
only when, one is true and the other false, and that two propositions
are equivalent when, and only when, both are true or both false.
It follows (<a href="#_5_24" class="pginternal">*5·24</a>) that the negation of "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p . q .\lor. {\sim}p . {\sim}q\)" src="images/1078.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 13.411ex; height: 1.792ex;" id="img_images_1078.svg">" is equivalent to "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p . {\sim}q .\lor. q .{\sim}p\)" src="images/1079.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 13.411ex; height: 1.792ex;" id="img_images_1079.svg">."
*5·54·55 state that both the product and the sum of <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_250"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_170"> are
equivalent, respectively, either to <img alt="" data-tex="\(p\)" src="images/39.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.138ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_39.svg_251"> or to <img alt="" data-tex="\(q\)" src="images/32.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.041ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_32.svg_171">.</p>

<p>The proofs of the following propositions are all easy, and we shall
therefore often merely indicate the propositions used in the proofs.</p>

<p>From <a href="#_5_25" class="pginternal">*5·25</a> it appears that we might have taken implication, instead of
disjunction, as a primitive idea, and have defined "<img alt="" data-tex="\(p\lor q\)" src="images/1098.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 4.693ex; height: 1.792ex;" id="img_images_1098.svg">" as

more primitive propositions than are required by the method we have
adopted.</p>

<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin {array}{l} \vdash.\text{*5·41}.\supset \vdash\colon\colon p\supset q.\supset .&amp;p\supset r:\equiv :p.\supset .q\supset r\colon\ldotp \\ &amp; p\supset r.\supset .p\supset q:\equiv :p.\supset .r\supset q &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*4·38}.\supset \vdash\colon\colon p\supset q.&amp;\equiv .p\supset r.\equiv \colon\ldotp p.\supset .q\supset r:p.\supset .r\supset q\colon\ldotp\\ [\text{*4·76}] &amp;\equiv \colon\ldotp p.\supset .q\equiv r\colon\colon \supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1124.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 71.207ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_1124.svg"></span></p>

<b>*5·75.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp r\supset {\sim}q:p.\equiv .q\lor r:\supset :p.{\sim}q.\equiv .r\)" src="images/1125.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 35.617ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_1125.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin {array}{l} \vdash.\text{*5·6}. &amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.\supset :p.{\sim}q.\supset .r &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{*3·27}.&amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.\supset :q\lor r.\supset .p:\\ [\text{*4·77}] &amp;\supset :r\supset p &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{*3·26}.&amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.\supset :r\supset {\sim}q &amp;\qquad \text{(3)}\\ \vdash.\text{(2).(3).Comp}.&amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.\supset :r\supset p.r\supset {\sim}q:\\ [\text{Comp}] &amp;\supset :r.\supset .p.{\sim}q &amp;\qquad \text{(4)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).(4).Comp}.&amp;\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.\supset :p.{\sim}q.\equiv .r\colon\ldotp \supset \vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/1126.svg" style="vertical-align: -10.068ex; width: 60.754ex; height: 21.267ex;" id="img_images_1126.svg"></span></p>
