<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_255">[Pg 255]</span></p>

<h2 class="nobreak" id="_32">*32. REFERENTS AND RELATA OF A GIVEN TERM WITH RESPECT
TO A GIVEN RELATION.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *32.</p>

<p>Given any relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_109">, the class of terms which have the relation
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_110"> to a given term <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_163"> are called the <i>referents</i> of <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_164">,
and the class of terms to which a given term <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_408"> has the relation
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_111"> are called the <i>relata</i> of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_409">. We shall denote by
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/349.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_349.svg_1"> the relation of the class of referents of <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_165">
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_166">, and by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/350.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.451ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_350.svg_1"> the relation of the class of
relata of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_410"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_411">. It is convenient also to have a notation
for the relations of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/349.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_349.svg_2"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/350.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.451ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_350.svg_2">
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_112">. We shall denote the relation of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/349.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_349.svg_3">
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_113"> by "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sg}\)" src="images/353.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 2.023ex; height: 1.491ex;" id="img_images_353.svg_2">," where "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sg}\)" src="images/353.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 2.023ex; height: 1.491ex;" id="img_images_353.svg_3">" stands for
"sagitta." Similarly we shall denote by "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{gs}\)" src="images/354.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 2.023ex; height: 1.491ex;" id="img_images_354.svg_1">" the relation
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/350.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.451ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_350.svg_3"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_114">, to suggest an arrow running from
right to left instead of from left to right. <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/349.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_349.svg_4">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/350.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.451ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_350.svg_4"> are chiefly useful for the sake
of the descriptive functions to which they give rise; thus
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy = \hat{x}(xRy)\)" src="images/2554.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 14.375ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2554.svg"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx= \hat{y}(xRy)\)" src="images/2555.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 15.108ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2555.svg">.
Thus <i>e.g.</i> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_115"> is the relation of
parent to son, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy =\)" src="images/2556.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.572ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2556.svg"> the parents of <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_167">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx =\)" src="images/2557.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.491ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_2557.svg"> the sons of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_412">. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_116"> is the relation
of less to greater among numbers of any kind, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy =\)" src="images/2556.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.572ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2556.svg_1">
numbers less than <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_168">, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx =\)" src="images/2557.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.491ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_2557.svg_1"> numbers
greater than <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_413">. When <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_30"> exists, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/343.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_343.svg_3"> is
the class whose only member is <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_31">. But when there are many terms
having the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_117"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_169">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/343.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_343.svg_4">, which is
the class of those terms, supplies a notation which cannot be supplied
by <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_32">. And similarly if there are many terms to which <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_414"> has
the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_118">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx\)" src="images/344.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.102ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_344.svg_4"> supplies the notation for
these terms. Thus for example let <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_119"> be the relation "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\sin\)" src="images/2428.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 2.778ex; height: 1.538ex;" id="img_images_2428.svg_1">,"
<i>i.e.</i> the relation which <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_415"> has to <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_170"> when <img alt="" data-tex="\(x = \sin y\)" src="images/2429.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 8.575ex; height: 1.977ex;" id="img_images_2429.svg_1">.
Then "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{\sin}ʻx\)" src="images/2558.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.807ex; height: 3.934ex;" id="img_images_2558.svg">" represents all values of <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_171">
such that <img alt="" data-tex="\(x = \sin y\)" src="images/2429.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 8.575ex; height: 1.977ex;" id="img_images_2429.svg_2">, <i>i.e.</i> all values of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\sin^{-1}x\)" src="images/2559.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 6.682ex; height: 1.986ex;" id="img_images_2559.svg"> or
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\arcsin x\)" src="images/2560.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 7.472ex; height: 1.538ex;" id="img_images_2560.svg">. Unlike the usual symbol, it is not ambiguous, since
instead of representing some one of these values, it represents the
class of them.</p>

<p>The definitions of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/349.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_349.svg_5">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/350.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.451ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_350.svg_5">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sg}\)" src="images/353.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 2.023ex; height: 1.491ex;" id="img_images_353.svg_4">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{gs}\)" src="images/354.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 2.023ex; height: 1.491ex;" id="img_images_354.svg_2"> are as follows:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R} = \hat{\alpha}\hat{y}\{\alpha = \hat{x}(xRy)\} \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2561.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 25.876ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2561.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R} = \hat{\beta}\hat{x}\{\beta = \hat{y}(xRy)\} \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2562.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.275ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2562.svg"></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_256">[Pg 256]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·03.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sg} = \hat{A}\hat{R}(A = \overrightarrow{R}) \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2563.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 21.328ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2563.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·04.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{gs} = \hat{A}\hat{R}(A = \overleftarrow{R}) \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2564.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 22.062ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2564.svg"></p>

<p>In virtue of the above definitions, we shall have <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sg}ʻR =\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/2565.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 9.832ex; height: 3.656ex;" id="img_images_2565.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{gs}ʻR=\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/2566.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 10.565ex; height: 3.656ex;" id="img_images_2566.svg">. This gives an
alternative notation which is convenient in dealing with a relation not
represented by a single letter.</p>

<p>It should be observed that if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_120"> is a homogeneous relation
(<i>i.e.</i> one in which referents and relata are of the same
type), then <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/349.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_349.svg_6"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/350.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.451ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_350.svg_6"> are not
homogeneous, but relate a class to objects of the type of its members.</p>

<p>In virtue of the definitions of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/349.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_349.svg_7"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/350.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.451ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_350.svg_7">, we shall have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·13.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash. \overrightarrow{R}ʻy = \hat{x}(xRy)\)" src="images/2567.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.763ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2567.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·131.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash. \overleftarrow{R}ʻx = \hat{y}(xRy)\)" src="images/2568.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 17.497ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2568.svg"></p>

<p>Thus by <a href="#_14_21" class="pginternal">*14·21</a>, we always have <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2569.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.353ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2569.svg">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\overleftarrow{R}ʻx\)" src="images/2570.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.272ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_2570.svg">. Thus whatever relation
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_121"> may be, we have <img alt="" data-tex="\((y).\text{E}!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2571.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.228ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2571.svg">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\((x).\text{E}!\overleftarrow{R}ʻx\)" src="images/2572.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.333ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2572.svg">. We do not in general
have <img alt="" data-tex="\((y). \exists! \overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2573.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 9.945ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2573.svg"> or (<img alt="" data-tex="\(x). \exists!\overleftarrow{R}ʻx\)" src="images/2574.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 10.17ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2574.svg">.
Thus taking <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_122"> to be the relation of parent and child,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy = \text{the parents of} ~ y\)" src="images/2575.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 22.282ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2575.svg"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx = \text{the children of} ~ x\)" src="images/2576.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 24.004ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_2576.svg">. Thus
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx = \Lambda\)" src="images/2577.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.69ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_2577.svg">, <i>i.e.</i>
<img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}\exists! \overleftarrow{R}ʻx\)" src="images/2578.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.75ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_2578.svg"> when <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_416"> is childless, and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy = \Lambda\)" src="images/2579.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 8.77ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2579.svg">, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}\exists!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2580.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 7.83ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2580.svg">,
when <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_172"> is Adam or Eve. The two sorts
of existence, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2569.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.353ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2569.svg_1"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2581.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.07ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2581.svg">,
can both be <i>significantly</i> predicated
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/343.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_343.svg_5">, because "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/343.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_343.svg_6">" is a
descriptive function whose value is a class; and the same applies to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx\)" src="images/344.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.102ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_344.svg_5">. It will be seen that (by *14·21)
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy .\supset. \text{E}!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2582.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 16.195ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2582.svg">,
but the converse implication does not hold in general.</p>

<p>We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·16.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: \overrightarrow{R} = \overrightarrow{S} .\equiv. \overleftarrow{R} = \overleftarrow{S} .\equiv. R = S\)" src="images/2583.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 30.545ex; height: 3.425ex;" id="img_images_2583.svg"></p>

<p>Also by *32·18·181,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash: x \in \overrightarrow{R}ʻy .\equiv. xRy .\equiv. y \in \overleftarrow{R}ʻx\text{.} \]" src="images/2584.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 32.154ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2584.svg"></span></p>

<p>Thus by the use of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/343.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_343.svg_7"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx\)" src="images/344.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.102ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_344.svg_6">,
every statement of the form "<img alt="" data-tex="\(xRy\)" src="images/266.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.12ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_266.svg_5">" can be reduced to a statement
asserting membership of a class. Since, however, the class in question
is given by a descriptive function, and descriptive functions are
defined by means of relations, we do not thus obtain a method of
reducing the theory of relations to the theory of classes.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R} = \hat{\beta}\hat{x}\{\beta = \hat{y}(xRy)\} \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2562.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.275ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2562.svg_1"></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_257">[Pg 257]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·03.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{sg}=\hat{A}\hat{R}(A=\overrightarrow{R}) \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/2586.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 21.328ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2586.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·04.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{gs}=\hat{A}\hat{R}(A=\overleftarrow{R}) \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/2587.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 22.062ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2587.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·1.</b>   <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:\alpha\overrightarrow{R}y.\equiv.\alpha=\hat{x}(xRy) \quad[\text{*21·3.(*32·01)}]\)" src="images/2588.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 39.673ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2588.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·101.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:\beta\overleftarrow{R}x.\equiv.\beta=\hat{y}(xRy) \quad[\text{*21·3.(*32·02)}]\)" src="images/2589.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 40.072ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2589.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·11.</b>  <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\hat{x}(xRy)=\overrightarrow{R}ʻy \quad[\text{*32·1.*30·3}]\)" src="images/2590.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.22ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2590.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·111.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\hat{y}(xRy)=\overleftarrow{R}ʻx \quad[\text{*32·101.*30·3}]\)" src="images/2591.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 34.216ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2591.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·12.</b>  <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\text{E}!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy \quad[\text{*32·11.*14·21}]\)" src="images/2592.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 25.461ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2592.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·121.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\text{E}!\overleftarrow{R}ʻx \quad[\text{*32·111.*14·21}]\)" src="images/2593.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.511ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2593.svg"></p>

<p>"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2569.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.353ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2569.svg_2">" must not be confounded with
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists !\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2594.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.07ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2594.svg">." The former means that there is
such a class as <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/343.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_343.svg_8">, which, as we have just seen,
is always true; the latter means that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/343.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_343.svg_9"> is
not null, which is only true if <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_173"> is a term to which some other
term has the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_123">. Note that, by <a href="#_14_21" class="pginternal">*14·21</a>, both <img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2581.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.07ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2581.svg_1">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}\exists !\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2595.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 7.83ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2595.svg">
imply <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2569.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.353ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2569.svg_3">. The contradictory of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2581.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.07ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2581.svg_2">
is not <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}\exists !\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2595.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 7.83ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2595.svg_1">,
but <img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}\{[\overrightarrow{R}ʻy].\exists !\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\}\)" src="images/2596.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.54ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2596.svg">.
This last would not imply <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2569.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.353ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2569.svg_4">, but for
the fact that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\overrightarrow{R}ʻy\)" src="images/2569.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 6.353ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_2569.svg_5"> is always true.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·131.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\overleftarrow{R}ʻx=\hat{y}(xRy) \quad[\text{*32·111.*20·59}]\)" src="images/2598.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.347ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2598.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·132.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:\alpha\overrightarrow{R}y.\equiv.\alpha=\overrightarrow{R}ʻy.\equiv.\alpha=\hat{x}(xRy) \quad[\text{*32·1·13.*20·57}]\)" src="images/2599.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 53.225ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2599.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*32·133.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:\beta\overleftarrow{R}x.\equiv.\beta=\overleftarrow{R}ʻx.\equiv.\beta=\hat{y}(xRy) \quad[\text{*32·101·131.*20·57}]\)" src="images/2600.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 57.77ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2600.svg"></p>

<p>The use of <a href="#_20_57" class="pginternal">*20·57</a> will in general be tacit. It happens constantly that
we have propositions such as *32·13, in which a descriptive expression
is shown to be identical with a class. In such cases, whenever the
properties of the class are asserted of the descriptive expression,
*20·57 is relevant.</p>

<h2 class="nobreak" id="_33">*33. DOMAINS, CONVERSE DOMAINS, AND FIELDS OF RELATIONS.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *33.</p>

<p>If <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_124"> is any relation, the <i>domain</i> of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_125">, which we denote
by <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_358.svg_2">, is the class of terms which have the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_126">
to something or other; the <i>converse domain</i>, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_360.svg_2">,
is the class of terms to which something or other has the relation
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_127">; and the <i>field</i>, <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR\)" src="images/362.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_362.svg_2">, is the sum of the domain and the
converse domain. (Note that the field is only significant when <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_128"> is
a <i>homogeneous</i> relation.)</p>

<p>The above notations <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_358.svg_3">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_360.svg_3">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR\)" src="images/362.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_362.svg_3"> are
derivative from the notations <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}\)" src="images/2636.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.729ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_2636.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}\)" src="images/2637.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2637.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(C\)" src="images/42.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.719ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_42.svg_1"> for the
relations, to a relation, of its domain, converse domain, and field
respectively. We are to have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{align} \text{D}ʻR &amp;= \hat{x}\{(\exists y).xRy\}\\ \text{ᗡ}ʻR &amp;= \hat{y}\{(\exists x).xRy\}\\ CʻR &amp;= \hat{x}\{(\exists y):xRy .\lor. yRx\}\text{;}\\ \end{align} \]" src="images/2638.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.71ex; width: 29.779ex; height: 8.552ex;" id="img_images_2638.svg"></span>
hence we define <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}\)" src="images/2636.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.729ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_2636.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}\)" src="images/2637.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2637.svg_1">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(C\)" src="images/42.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.719ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_42.svg_2"> as follows:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D} = \hat{\alpha}\hat{R}[\alpha = \hat{x}\{(\exists y).xRy\}] \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2639.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.126ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_2639.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ} = \hat{\beta}\hat{R}[\beta = \hat{y}\{(\exists x).xRy\}] \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2640.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 30.42ex; height: 2.993ex;" id="img_images_2640.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·03.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(C = \hat{\gamma}\hat{R}[\gamma = \hat{x}\{(\exists y):xRy .\lor. yRx\}] \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2641.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 39.199ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_2641.svg"></p>

<p>The letter <img alt="" data-tex="\(C\)" src="images/42.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.719ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_42.svg_3"> is chosen as the initial of the word "campus." We
require one other definition, namely of the relation of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_419"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_129">
when <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_420"> is a member of the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_130">. This relation, which we
will call <img alt="" data-tex="\(F\)" src="images/45.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.695ex; height: 1.538ex;" id="img_images_45.svg_5">, is defined as follows:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·04.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(F = \hat{x}\hat{R}\{(\exists y):xRy .\lor. yRx\} \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2642.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 32.442ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_2642.svg"></p>

<p>We shall find that <img alt="" data-tex="\(C = \overrightarrow{F}\)" src="images/2643.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 6.431ex; height: 3.369ex;" id="img_images_2643.svg">. <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{\text{D}}\)" src="images/2644.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.729ex; height: 2.414ex;" id="img_images_2644.svg">
will be the relation of a relation to its domain,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{\text{D}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/2645.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.068ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_2645.svg"> will be the class of relations
having <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_110"> for their domain. Similar remarks apply to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}\)" src="images/2637.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2637.svg_2"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(C\)" src="images/42.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.719ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_42.svg_4">. The <i>field</i> of a relation is specially
important in connection with series.</p>

<p>The propositions of this number are constantly used throughout the
remainder of the work. The ideas of the domain, converse domain, and
field are very general, and have somewhat different uses for relations
of different<span class="pagenum" id="Page_261">[Pg 261]</span> kinds. Consider first the sort of relation that gives
rise to a descriptive function <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_33">. For this we require that
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_34"> should exist whenever there is anything having the relation
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_131"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_176">, <i>i.e.</i> that there should never be more than one
term having the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_132"> to a given term <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_177">. In this case,
the values of <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_178"> for which <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_35"> exists will constitute the
"converse domain" of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_133">, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_360.svg_4">, and the values
which <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_36"> assumes for various values of <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_179"> will constitute
the "domain" of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_134">, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_358.svg_4">. Thus the converse
domain is the class of possible arguments for the descriptive function
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_37">, and the domain is the class of all values of the function.
Thus, for example, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_135"> is the relation of the square of an integer
<img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_180"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_181">, then <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_38">=the square of <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_182">, provided <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_183"> is
an integer. In this case, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_360.svg_5"> is the class of integers,
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_358.svg_5"> is the class of perfect squares. Or again, suppose
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_136"> is the relation of wife to husband; then <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_39">=the wife of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_184">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_360.svg_6">=married men, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_358.svg_6">=married women. In
such cases, the <i>field</i> usually has little importance; and if
the values of the function <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_40"> are not of the same type as its
arguments, <i>i.e.</i> if the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_137"> is not <i>homogeneous</i>,
the field is meaningless. Thus, for example, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_138"> is a homogeneous
relation, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/349.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_349.svg_8"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/350.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.451ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_350.svg_8"> are
not homogeneous, and therefore "<img alt="" data-tex="\(Cʻ\overrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/2646.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_2646.svg">" and
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(Cʻ\overleftarrow{R}\)" src="images/2647.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.528ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_2647.svg">" are meaningless.</p>

<p>Let us next suppose that <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_139"> is the sort of relation that generates
a series, say the relation of less to greater among integers. Then
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_358.svg_7">= all integers that are less than some other integer =
all integers, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_360.svg_7">= all integers that are greater than some
other integer = all integers except 0. In this case, <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR\)" src="images/362.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_362.svg_4">= all
integers that are either greater or less than some other integer = all
integers. Generally, if <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_140"> generates a series, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_358.svg_8"> = all
members of the series except the last (if any), <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_360.svg_8"> = all
members of the series except the first (if any), and <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR\)" src="images/362.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_362.svg_5"> = all
members of the series. In this case, "<img alt="" data-tex="\(xFR\)" src="images/2648.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 4.706ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_2648.svg">" expresses the fact that
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_421"> is a member of the series. Thus when <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_141"> generates a series,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR\)" src="images/362.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_362.svg_6"> becomes important, and the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(F\)" src="images/45.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.695ex; height: 1.538ex;" id="img_images_45.svg_6"> is likely to be
useful.</p>

<p>We shall have occasion to deal with many relations having some of
the properties of series, and with many propositions which, though
only important in connection with serial relations, hold much more
generally. In such cases, the field of a relation is likely to be
important. Thus in the section on Induction (Part II, <a href="#SECTION_E_b" class="pginternal">Section E</a>), where
we are preparing the way for the construction of serial relations
by means of a certain kind of non-serial relation, and throughout
relation-arithmetic (Part IV), the fields of relations will occur
constantly. But in the earlier parts of the work, it is chiefly domains
and converse domains that occur.</p>

<p>Among the more important properties of domains, converse domains and
fields, which are proved in the present number, are the following.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_262">[Pg 262]</span></p>

<p>We have always <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2649.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.973ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2649.svg">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/2650.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.602ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2650.svg">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!CʻR\)" src="images/2651.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.964ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2651.svg"> (*33·12·121·122). (The last of these, however, is only
significant when <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_142"> is homogeneous.)</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·13.</b>  <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:x\in \text{D}ʻR.\equiv.(\exists y).xRy\)" src="images/2652.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 24.528ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2652.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·131.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:y\in \text{ᗡ}ʻR.\equiv.(\exists x).xRy\)" src="images/2653.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 24.157ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2653.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·132.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp x\in CʻR.\equiv:(\exists y):xRy.\lor .yRx\)" src="images/2654.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 34.046ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2654.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·14.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:xRy.\supset.x\in \text{D}ʻR.y\in \text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/2655.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 28.708ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_2655.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·16.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.CʻR=\text{D}ʻR\cup \text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/2656.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 21.949ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2656.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·2·21·22.</b> The converse domain of a relation is the domain of
its converse, the domain of a relation is the converse domain of its
converse, and the field of a relation is the field of its converse.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·24.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:\exists !\text{D}ʻR.\equiv.\exists !\text{ᗡ}ʻR.\equiv.\exists !CʻR.\equiv.\dot{\exists}!R\)" src="images/2657.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 37.251ex; height: 2.758ex;" id="img_images_2657.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·4.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\text{D}ʻR=\hat{x}\{\exists !\overleftarrow{R}ʻx\}\)" src="images/2658.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 20.755ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_2658.svg"></p>

<p>with corresponding propositions (*33·41·42) for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_360.svg_9"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻR\)" src="images/362.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.794ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_362.svg_7">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·43.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:\text{E}!Rʻy.\supset.y\in \text{ᗡ}ʻR.Rʻy\in \text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2659.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 33.83ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_2659.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*33·431.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:(y).\text{E}!Rʻy.\supset.(\beta).\beta\subset\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/2660.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 29.416ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2660.svg"></p>

<p>If <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_143"> is the sort of relation which generates a series,
so that "<img alt="" data-tex="\(xRy\)" src="images/266.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.12ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_266.svg_8">" may be read "<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_422"> precedes <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_185">," then
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\subset\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/2694.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.252ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2694.svg"> is the condition that the series may<span class="pagenum" id="Page_264">[Pg 264]</span>
have no last term, since it states that every term which follows some
term precedes some other term, and is therefore not the last of the
series.</p>

<p>Note that by our conventions as to denoting expressions, the scope of
both <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_41"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Sʻy\)" src="images/2444.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 3.925ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_2444.svg_8"> in the above is "<img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy=Sʻy\)" src="images/2745.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 11.126ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_2745.svg">," and <img alt="" data-tex="\(Rʻy\)" src="images/326.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 4.183ex; height: 2.161ex;" id="img_images_326.svg_42"> is
to have the larger scope.</p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*33·41.Transp}. &amp;\supset\vdash:y{\sim}\in \text{ᗡ}ʻR\cup \text{ᗡ}ʻS. \supset\overrightarrow{R}ʻy=\Lambda.\overrightarrow{S}ʻy=\Lambda &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*13·172.*4·83}.&amp;\supset\vdash:\text{Hp}.\supset.(y).\overrightarrow{R}ʻy=\overrightarrow{S}ʻy.\\ [\text{*30·41}]                  &amp;\qquad\qquad\supset.\overrightarrow{R}=\overrightarrow{S}\\ [\text{*32·14}]                  &amp;\qquad\qquad\supset.R=S:\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2749.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.631ex; width: 74.517ex; height: 16.394ex;" id="img_images_2749.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*32·1}.\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp \alpha\overrightarrow{F}R.&amp;\equiv.\alpha=\hat{x}(xFR)\\ [\text{*33·103}]   &amp;=\hat{x}\{(\exists y):xRy.\lor .yRx\}\\ [\text{*33·102}]  &amp;\equiv.\alpha CR &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*11·11.*21·43}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2751.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.128ex; width: 64.739ex; height: 13.387ex;" id="img_images_2751.svg"></span></p>

a series generated by a relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_9">, and "<img alt="" data-tex="\(xFP\)" src="images/2753.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 4.688ex; height: 1.57ex;" id="img_images_2753.svg">" expresses the
fact that <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_423"> is a member of this series. The above two propositions
(*33·5·51) will be much used in Part IV, where we deal with the
foundations of ordinal arithmetic, but will not often be referred to
elsewhere.</p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_269">[Pg 269]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_34">*34. THE RELATIVE PRODUCT OF TWO RELATIONS.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *34.</p>

<p>The relative product of two relations <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_144"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/254.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_254.svg_23"> is the relation
which holds between <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_424"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_26"> when there is an intermediate term
<img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_186"> such that <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_425"> has the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_145"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_187"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_188"> has
the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/254.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_254.svg_24"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_27">. Thus <i>e.g.</i> the relative product
of <i>brother</i> and <i>father</i> is <i>paternal uncle</i>; the
relative product of <i>father</i> and <i>father</i> is <i>paternal
grandfather</i>; and so on. The relative product of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_146"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/254.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_254.svg_25"> is
denoted by "<img alt="" data-tex="\(R \mid S\)" src="images/370.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 5.062ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_370.svg_1">"; the definition is:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(R \mid S = \hat{x}\hat{z}\{(\exists y).xRy.ySz\} \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2758.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.25ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_2758.svg"></p>

<p>This definition is only significant when <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/360.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.432ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_360.svg_10"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻS\)" src="images/2759.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.545ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2759.svg"> belong to the same type.</p>

<p>The relative product of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_147"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_148"> is called the square of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_149">;
we put</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(R^{2} = R \mid R \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2760.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 15.725ex; height: 2.45ex;" id="img_images_2760.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·03.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(R^{3} = R^{2} \mid R \quad \text{Df}\)" src="images/2761.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 16.713ex; height: 2.45ex;" id="img_images_2761.svg"></p>

<p>The most useful propositions in the present number are the following:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash . \text{Cnv}ʻ(R \mid S) = \breve{S} \mid \breve{R}\)" src="images/2762.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 22.734ex; height: 3.029ex;" id="img_images_2762.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> the converse of a relative product is obtained by turning
each factor into its converse and reversing the order of the factors.</p>

<p class="nind"><b><a id="_34_21">*34·21</a>.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash . (P \mid Q) \mid R = P \mid (Q \mid R)\)" src="images/2763.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 26.881ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2763.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> the relative product obeys the associative law.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·25.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash . P \mid (Q\unicode{x228d}R) = (P \mid Q) \unicode{x228d} (P \mid R)\)" src="images/2764.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.169ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2764.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·26.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash . (P \unicode{x228d} Q) \mid R = (P \mid R) \unicode{x228d} (Q \mid R)\)" src="images/2765.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.188ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2765.svg"></p>

<p><i>I.e.</i> the relative product obeys the distributive law
with respect to the logical addition of relations. (For logical
multiplication instead of logical addition, we only get inclusion
instead of identity; cf. *34·23·24.)</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·34.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : R \unicode{x2abd} P . S \unicode{x2abd} Q .\supset. R \mid S \unicode{x2abd} P \mid Q\)" src="images/2766.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 28.593ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_2766.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·36.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash . \text{D}ʻ(P \mid Q) \subset \text{D}ʻP.\text{ᗡ}ʻ(P \mid Q)\subset\text{ᗡ}ʻQ\)" src="images/2767.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 38.789ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2767.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·41.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash : \text{E}!PʻQʻz .\supset. PʻQʻz = (P \mid Q)ʻz\)" src="images/2768.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.654ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2768.svg"></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_270">[Pg 270]</span></p>

<hr class="tb">

<p class="nind"><b>*34·01.</b><img alt="" data-tex="\( R\mid S=\hat{x}\hat{z}\{(\exists y).xRy.ySz\} \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/2769.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.25ex; height: 2.398ex;" id="img_images_2769.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(R^{2}=R\mid R \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/2770.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 15.725ex; height: 2.45ex;" id="img_images_2770.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·03.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(R^{3}=R^{2}\mid R \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/2771.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 16.713ex; height: 2.45ex;" id="img_images_2771.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·1.</b>  <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:x(R\mid S)z.\equiv.(\exists y).xRy.ySz \quad[\text{*21·3.(*34·01)}]\)" src="images/2772.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 46.808ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2772.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*34·1.*32·18·181}.\supset\\ \vdash:x(R\mid S)z.&amp;\equiv.(\exists y).y\in \overleftarrow{R}ʻx.y\in \overrightarrow{S}ʻz.\\ [\text{*22·33}] &amp; \equiv.(\exists y).y\in \overleftarrow{R}ʻx\cap \overrightarrow{S}ʻz.\\ [\text{*24·5}]  &amp; \equiv.\exists !(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx\cap \overrightarrow{S}ʻz):\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2774.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.631ex; width: 51.629ex; height: 16.394ex;" id="img_images_2774.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·2.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\text{Cnv}ʻ(R\mid S)=\breve{S}\mid \breve{R}\)" src="images/2776.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 22.734ex; height: 3.029ex;" id="img_images_2776.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*31·131}.\supset\vdash:x\{\text{Cnv}ʻ(R\mid S)\}z.&amp;\equiv.z(R\mid S)x.\\ [\text{*34·1}] &amp;\equiv.(\exists y).zRy.ySx.\\ [\text{*34·11}] &amp;\equiv.(\exists y).y\breve{R}z.x\breve{S}y.\\ [\text{*34·1}] &amp;\equiv.x(\breve{S}\mid \breve{R})z &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*11·11.*21·43}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2777.svg" style="vertical-align: -7.667ex; width: 61.929ex; height: 16.466ex;" id="img_images_2777.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*31·131}.\supset\vdash:x(\text{Cnv}ʻ\breve{R})y.ySz.&amp;\equiv.y\breve{R}x.ySz.\\ [\text{*31·11}]  &amp;\equiv.xRy.ySz &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*10·11·281.*34·1}.\supset\vdash:x\{(\text{Cnv}ʻ\breve{R})\mid S\}z.&amp;\equiv.x(R\mid S)z &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(2).*11·11.*21·43}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2779.svg" style="vertical-align: -6.034ex; width: 68.991ex; height: 13.199ex;" id="img_images_2779.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·203.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.R\mid S=R\mid (\text{Cnv}ʻ\breve{S}) \quad[\text{Similar proof}]\)" src="images/2780.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 38.967ex; height: 3.029ex;" id="img_images_2780.svg"></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*34·1.*10·281}.\supset\vdash\colon\colon(\exists z).x(P\mid Q)z.zRw.&amp;\equiv\colon\ldotp (\exists z):(\exists y).xPy.yQz:zRw\colon\ldotp \\ [\text{*11·6}] &amp;\equiv\colon\ldotp (\exists y)\colon\ldotp xPy:(\exists z).yQz.zRw\colon\ldotp \\ [\text{*34·1.*10·281}] &amp; \equiv\colon\ldotp (\exists y).xPy.y(Q\mid R)w &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*11·11.*34·1.*21·43}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2782.svg" style="vertical-align: -5.317ex; width: 86.226ex; height: 11.765ex;" id="img_images_2782.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·22.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\mid Q\mid R=(P\mid Q)\mid R \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/2783.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.416ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2783.svg"></p>

<p>This definition serves merely for the avoidance of brackets.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_271">[Pg 271]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·23.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.P\mid (Q\dot{\cap}R)\unicode{x2abd}(P\mid Q)\dot{\cap}(P\mid R)\)" src="images/2784.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 29.813ex; height: 2.654ex;" id="img_images_2784.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{34·1}.\supset \vdash\colon\ldotp x\{P\mid (Q\dot{\cap}R)\}y.&amp;\equiv:(\exists z).xPz.z(Q\dot{\cap}R)y:\\ [\text{*23·33}]  &amp;\equiv:(\exists z).xPz.zQy.zRy:\\ [\text{*10·5}]  &amp;\supset:(\exists z).xPz.zQy:(\exists z).xPz.zRy:\\ [\text{*34·1}] &amp;\supset:x(P\mid Q)y.x(P\mid R)y:\\ [\text{*23·33}] &amp;\supset:x\{(P\mid Q)\dot{\cap}(P\mid R)\}y &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*11·11}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2785.svg" style="vertical-align: -8.876ex; width: 74.412ex; height: 18.882ex;" id="img_images_2785.svg"></span></p>

<p>The converse of the above is not true.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·24.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.(P\dot{\cap}Q)\mid R\unicode{x2abd}(P\mid R)\dot{\cap}(Q\mid R) \quad[\text{Similar proof}]\)" src="images/2786.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 46.064ex; height: 2.654ex;" id="img_images_2786.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·25.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.P\mid (Q\unicode{x228d}R)=(P\mid Q)\unicode{x228d}(P\mid R)\)" src="images/2787.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.169ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2787.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*23·34.*10·281}.\supset\\ \vdash\colon\ldotp (\exists z).xPz.z(Q\unicode{x228d}R)y.&amp;\equiv:(\exists z):xPz:zQy.\lor .zRy:\\ [\text{*4·4.*10·281}]  &amp;\equiv:(\exists z):xPz.zQy.\lor .xPz.zRy:\\ [\text{*10·42}] &amp; \equiv:(\exists z).xPz.zQy:\lor :(\exists z).xPz.zRy:\\ [\text{*34·1}] &amp;\equiv:x(P\mid Q)y.\lor .x(P\mid R)y:\\ [\text{*23·34}]  &amp;\equiv:x(P\mid Q\unicode{x228d}P\mid R)y &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*11·11.*34·1}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/2788.svg" style="vertical-align: -10.068ex; width: 77.528ex; height: 21.267ex;" id="img_images_2788.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·26.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.(P\unicode{x228d}Q)\mid R=(P\mid R)\unicode{x228d}(Q\mid R) \quad[\text{Similar proof}]\)" src="images/2789.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 47.421ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2789.svg"></p>

<p>The above two forms of the distributive law, and the associative law
(<a href="#_34_21" class="pginternal">*34·21</a>), are the only ones of the usual formal laws that hold for the
relative product. The commutative law, in particular, does not hold in
general.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*34·27.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:R=R'.\supset.R\mid P=R'\mid P\)" src="images/2790.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 27.74ex; height: 2.28ex;" id="img_images_2790.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_272">[Pg 272]</span></p>

<p>In proving the equality of two relations, say <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_150"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/254.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_254.svg_26">, we
usually establish first an asserted proposition of the form
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} xRy.&amp;\equiv.xSy\\ \text{or}\qquad\qquad \text{Hp}.\supset:xRy.&amp;\equiv.xSy. \end{aligned} \]" src="images/2795.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 30.681ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_2795.svg"></span></p>

<p>We then proceed by <a href="#_11_11" class="pginternal">*11·11</a> (together with <a href="#_11_3" class="pginternal">*11·3</a> in the second case) to
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ (x,y):xRy.\equiv.xSy\, \text{or Hp}.\supset:(x,y):xRy.\equiv.xSy, \]" src="images/2796.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 48.187ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2796.svg"></span>
whence the result follows by <a href="#_21_43" class="pginternal">*21·43</a>. We shall in future omit these
steps, and write "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\supset\vdash.\text{Prop}\)" src="images/815.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 8.965ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_815.svg_1">" after we have
established
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ xRy.\equiv.xSy\, \text{or Hp}.\supset:xRy.\equiv.xSy. \]" src="images/2797.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 34.077ex; height: 2.059ex;" id="img_images_2797.svg"></span>
A similar ellipsis will be made in proving the equality of classes.</p>

<p>The above proposition is no longer true if we change the hypothesis
into <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{E}!(P\mid Q)ʻz\)" src="images/2823.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 11.714ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2823.svg">, since (<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\mid Q)ʻz\)" src="images/2824.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 8.664ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2824.svg"> may exist when
<img alt="" data-tex="\(PʻQʻz\)" src="images/2825.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.256ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2825.svg"> does not. Suppose, <i>e.g.</i>, that <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/2826.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_2826.svg">is the relation
of child to father, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_10"> the relation of daughter to father.
Then (<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\mid Q)ʻz\)" src="images/2824.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 8.664ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2824.svg_1">= the granddaughter of <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_28">, but <img alt="" data-tex="\(PʻQʻz\)" src="images/2825.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.256ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_2825.svg_1">= the
daughter of the child of <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_29">. The first exists whenever <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_30"> has
only one granddaughter, while the second requires further that <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_31">
should have only one child.</p>

<p>For the same reason we do not have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ b=(P\mid Q)ʻz.\supset.(\exists c).b=Pʻc.c=Qʻz. \]" src="images/2827.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 40.163ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_2827.svg"></span>
This will hold if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_11">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/2826.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_2826.svg_1"> are one-many relations (cf. <a href="#_71" class="pginternal">*71</a>), but
not in general otherwise.</p>

be regarded as expressing equality in some respect.</p>
