<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_585">[Pg 585]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_91">*91. ON POWERS OF A RELATION.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *91.</p>

<p>In the present number, we consider the class of relations
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R, R^{2}, R^{3}, \ldots \]" src="images/6692.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 12.797ex; height: 2.439ex;" id="img_images_6692.svg"></span></p>

<p>Each of these has to its predecessor the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mid R\)" src="images/3692.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 2.975ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_3692.svg_2">; we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R^{2} = \mid RʻR, R^{3} = \mid RʻR^{2}, \text{etc.} \]" src="images/6693.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 28.803ex; height: 2.563ex;" id="img_images_6693.svg"></span>
Thus every term of the series has to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_297"> the relation (<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mid R)_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6694.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 4.842ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6694.svg">; hence the powers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_298"> may be defined
as those relations which have to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_299"> the relation (<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mid R)_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6694.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 4.842ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6694.svg_1">. The series of powers starting with <img alt="" data-tex="\(I \upharpoonright CʻR\)" src="images/6695.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.135ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6695.svg"> instead of with <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_300"> is similarly composed of
those relations which have to <img alt="" data-tex="\(I \upharpoonright CʻR\)" src="images/6696.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.135ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6696.svg"> the relation
<img alt="" data-tex="\((\mid R)_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6520.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 5.722ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6520.svg_1">. (This class consists of the previous
class together with <img alt="" data-tex="\(I \upharpoonright CʻR\)" src="images/6696.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.135ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6696.svg_1">.) To say that the
relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6488.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.283ex; width: 2.705ex; height: 1.829ex;" id="img_images_6488.svg_7"> holds between <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_558"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_263"> turns
out to be equivalent to saying that one of the relations
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ I \upharpoonright CʻR,\quad R,\quad R^{2},\quad R^{3},\, \ldots \]" src="images/6697.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 29.103ex; height: 2.452ex;" id="img_images_6697.svg"></span>
holds between <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_559"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_264">; and to say that the relation
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R \mid R_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6698.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 6.308ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_6698.svg"> holds between <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_560"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_265">
turns out to be equivalent to saying that one of the relations
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R,\quad R^{2},\quad R^{3}, \ldots \]" src="images/6699.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 17.322ex; height: 2.439ex;" id="img_images_6699.svg"></span>
holds between <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_561"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_266">. Thus we might have begun by defining
powers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_301">, and proceeded to define <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6488.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.283ex; width: 2.705ex; height: 1.829ex;" id="img_images_6488.svg_8"> as
their sum.</p>

<p>For notational convenience we put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R_{\text{ts}} = (\mid R)_{\unicode{x2217}} \quad \text{Df}\text{.} \]" src="images/6700.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 17.209ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6700.svg"></span>
Then the definition of powers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_302"> excluding <img alt="" data-tex="\(I \upharpoonright CʻR\)" src="images/6696.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.135ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6696.svg_2"> is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Pot}ʻR = \overrightarrow{R}_{\text{ts}}ʻR \quad \text{Df}\text{,} \]" src="images/6701.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 21.188ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6701.svg"></span>
and the definition of powers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_303"> including <img alt="" data-tex="\(I \upharpoonright CʻR\)" src="images/6696.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.135ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6696.svg_3"> is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{Potid}ʻR = \overrightarrow{R}_{\text{ts}}ʻ(I \upharpoonright CʻR) \quad \text{Df}\text{.} \]" src="images/6702.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 31.253ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_6702.svg"></span>
(Here the letters "id" are added to suggest that identity is to be
added to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Pot}ʻR\)" src="images/6515.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.627ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6515.svg_3">.)</p>

<p>We put also
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R_{\text{po}}=\dot{s}ʻ\text{Pot}ʻR \quad \text{Df}\text{.} \]" src="images/6703.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 20.969ex; height: 2.385ex;" id="img_images_6703.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_586">[Pg 586]</span></p>

<p>Many of the propositions in this number are very often used. Among the
more important propositions are the following:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·17.</b>  <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp P\in \text{Potid}ʻR:\phi S.\supset_{S}.\phi(S\mid R):\phi(I\upharpoonright CʻR):\supset.\phi P\)" src="images/6704.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 54.43ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6704.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·171.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp P\in \text{Pot}ʻR:\phi S.\supset_{S}.\phi(S\mid R):\phi R:\supset.\phi P\)" src="images/6705.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 44.365ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6705.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·373.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp P\in \text{Pot}ʻR.\supset_{P}.\phi P:\equiv:\phi R:S\in \text{Pot}ʻR.\phi S.\supset_{S}.\phi(S\mid R)\)" src="images/6706.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 59.75ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6706.svg"></p>

<p>These are formulae of induction. The first two state that if the
property <img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi\)" src="images/55.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.348ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_55.svg_85"> is hereditary with respect to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mid R\)" src="images/3692.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 2.975ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_3692.svg_3">, then if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi\)" src="images/55.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.348ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_55.svg_86"> belongs to <img alt="" data-tex="\(I\upharpoonright CʻR\)" src="images/6508.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.135ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6508.svg_6"> it belongs to any member
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Potid}ʻR\)" src="images/6523.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.514ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6523.svg_1">, while if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi\)" src="images/55.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.348ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_55.svg_87"> belongs to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_304"> it belongs
to any member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Pot}ʻR\)" src="images/6515.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.627ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6515.svg_4">. The third gives a form of induction
which is sometimes more powerful than the second. It states that if
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi\)" src="images/55.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.348ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_55.svg_88"> is hereditary provided its argument is a power of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_305">, and
if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi R\)" src="images/6707.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 3.066ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_6707.svg">, then every power of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_306"> satisfies <img alt="" data-tex="\(\phi\)" src="images/55.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.348ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_55.svg_89">, and vice
versa.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·23.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\text{Potid}ʻR=\iotaʻ(I\upharpoonright CʻR)\cup \text{Pot}ʻR\)" src="images/6708.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 35.114ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6708.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·24.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\text{Pot}ʻR=\mid Rʻʻ\text{Potid}ʻR\)" src="images/6709.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 25.607ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_6709.svg"></p>

<p>These two propositions are very useful as giving relations of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Pot}ʻR\)" src="images/6515.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.627ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6515.svg_5"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Potid}ʻR\)" src="images/6523.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.514ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6523.svg_2">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·27.</b>  <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:P\in \text{Potid}ʻR.\supset.CʻP\subset CʻR\)" src="images/6710.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 31.978ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6710.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·271.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:P\in \text{Pot}ʻR.\supset.\text{D}ʻP\subset DʻR.\text{ᗡ}ʻP\subset \text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/6711.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 43.123ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6711.svg"></p>

<p>We do not have in general <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\in \text{Pot}ʻR.\supset.\text{D}ʻP=\text{D}ʻR.\text{ᗡ}ʻP=\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/6712.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 40.339ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6712.svg">.
If <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_307"> is the sort of relation which generates a series (<i>i.e.</i>
is either itself serial, or such that <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/6526.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.594ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_6526.svg_2"> is serial),
the above would characterize a series without a first or last term. To
illustrate the matter, consider a series of four terms, <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_562">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_267">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_50">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(w\)" src="images/263.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.62ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_263.svg_14">, and let <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_308"> be the relation of immediately preceding
in this series. Thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_309"> holds between <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_563"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_268">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_269"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_51">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_52"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(w\)" src="images/263.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.62ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_263.svg_15">. Then <img alt="" data-tex="\(R^{2}\)" src="images/6509.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.705ex; height: 1.934ex;" id="img_images_6509.svg_1"> holds between <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_564"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_53">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_270"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(w\)" src="images/263.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.62ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_263.svg_16">; thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_54">, which belongs to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/358.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.803ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_358.svg_18">, does not
belong to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR^{2}\)" src="images/6713.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.791ex; height: 2.339ex;" id="img_images_6713.svg">. <img alt="" data-tex="\(R^{3}\)" src="images/6714.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.705ex; height: 1.933ex;" id="img_images_6714.svg"> holds only between <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_565"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(w\)" src="images/263.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.62ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_263.svg_17">;
thus neither <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_271"> nor <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_55"> belongs to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻR^{3}\)" src="images/6715.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.791ex; height: 2.338ex;" id="img_images_6715.svg">. All powers
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_310"> beyond the third are null. On the other hand, if we take a
cyclic relation, such as that of left-hand neighbour at a dinner-table,
we shall always have <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻP=\text{D}ʻR.\text{ᗡ}ʻP=\text{ᗡ}ʻR\)" src="images/6716.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 25.475ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6716.svg">,
whatever power of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\, P\)" src="images/6717.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 3.794ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_6717.svg"> may be.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·282.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:P\in \text{Pot}ʻR.\supset.P\mid R\in \text{Pot}ʻR\)" src="images/6718.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 32.199ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_6718.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition shows that <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Pot}ʻR\)" src="images/6515.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.627ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6515.svg_6"> is a hereditary class with
respect to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\mid R\)" src="images/3692.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 2.975ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_3692.svg_4">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·34.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:P,\,Q\in \text{Potid}ʻR.\supset.P\mid Q=Q\mid P\)" src="images/6719.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 36.33ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_6719.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition states that the relative product is commutative when
each factor is <img alt="" data-tex="\(I\upharpoonright CʻR\)" src="images/6508.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.135ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6508.svg_7"> or a power of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_311">.</p>

<p>We come next to propositions concerning <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/6526.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.594ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_6526.svg_3">. We have</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·502.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.R\unicode{x2abd}R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/6720.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 9.057ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6720.svg"></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_587">[Pg 587]</span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·504.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\text{D}ʻR_{\text{po}}=\text{D}ʻR.\text{ᗡ}ʻR_{\text{po}}=\text{ᗡ}ʻR.CʻR_{\text{po}}=CʻR\)" src="images/6721.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 47.142ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6721.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·511.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.R_{\text{po}}\mid R\unicode{x2abd}R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/6722.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 14.538ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6722.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·52.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.R_{\text{po}}=R_{\unicode{x2217}}\mid R=R\mid R_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6723.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 24.633ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6723.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·54.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.R_{\unicode{x2217}}=I\upharpoonright CʻR\unicode{x228d}R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/6724.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 21.197ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6724.svg"></p>

<p>*91·52·54 are fundamental in the theory of inductive relations.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·542.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:xR_{\unicode{x2217}}y.x \neq y.\equiv.xR_{\text{po}}y.x \neq y\)" src="images/6725.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 30.368ex; height: 2.27ex;" id="img_images_6725.svg"></p>

<p>This proposition is particularly useful when (as often happens)
we have <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\unicode{x2abd}J\)" src="images/6726.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 6.384ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6726.svg">. In that case, it gives
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}=R_{\unicode{x2217}}\dot{\cap}J\)" src="images/6727.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 12.257ex; height: 2.738ex;" id="img_images_6727.svg">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·55.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.R_{\unicode{x2217}}=\dot{s}ʻ\text{Potid}ʻR\)" src="images/6728.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 19.042ex; height: 2.188ex;" id="img_images_6728.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·56.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.R_{\text{po}}^{2}\unicode{x2abd}R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/6729.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.869ex; width: 10.935ex; height: 2.756ex;" id="img_images_6729.svg"></p>

<p>Thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/6526.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.594ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_6526.svg_4"> is always transitive, which is one of the three
characteristics of serial relations (cf. *204). We shall find that
<img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/6526.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.594ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_6526.svg_5"> is often serial when <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_312"> is not so.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·574.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.R_{\unicode{x2217}}\mid R_{\text{po}}=R_{\text{po}}\mid R_{\unicode{x2217}}=R_{\text{po}}=R\mid     R_{\unicode{x2217}}=R_{\unicode{x2217}}\mid R\)" src="images/6730.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 47.037ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6730.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·602.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.(R_{\text{po}})_{\unicode{x2217}}=R_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6731.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 14.453ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6731.svg"></p>

<hr class="tb">

<p class="nind"><b>*91·01.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{st}}=(R\mid)_{\unicode{x2217}} \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6732.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.58ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6732.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·02.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{ts}}=(\mid R)_{\unicode{x2217}} \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6733.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 16.58ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6733.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·03.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Pot}ʻR=\overrightarrow{R}_{\text{ts}}ʻR \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6734.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 20.559ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6734.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·04.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Potid}ʻR=\overrightarrow{R}_{\text{ts}}ʻ(I\upharpoonright CʻR) \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6735.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 30.624ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_6735.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·05.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}=\dot{s}ʻ\text{Pot}ʻR \quad\text{Df}\)" src="images/6736.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 20.34ex; height: 2.385ex;" id="img_images_6736.svg"></p>

<p>The first two of the above definitions are introduced merely for
notational convenience. The other three represent ideas of great
importance. The last is especially useful when a series is given as the
field of a one-one relation between consecutive terms—as, <i>e.g.</i>,
when the series of natural numbers is given as the field of the
relation of <img alt="" data-tex="\(n\)" src="images/394.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.357ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_394.svg_50"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(n + 1\)" src="images/502.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 5.254ex; height: 1.692ex;" id="img_images_502.svg_2">. Then <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\text{po}}\)" src="images/6526.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 3.594ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_6526.svg_6"> is the relation
of any earlier term to any later term—<i>e.g.</i>, in the above case
of the natural numbers, the relation of a less integer to a greater.</p>

belongs to <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_314"> (or <img alt="" data-tex="\(I\upharpoonright CʻR\)" src="images/6508.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.135ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6508.svg_8">) and also belongs to
<img alt="" data-tex="\(S\mid R\)" src="images/6510.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 5.062ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_6510.svg_3"> whenever it belongs to <img alt="" data-tex="\(S\)" src="images/254.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.05ex; width: 1.459ex; height: 1.645ex;" id="img_images_254.svg_45">.</p>

<p>The last line of the above proof is obtained as follows: writing
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\mu\)" src="images/3357.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 1.364ex; height: 1.489ex;" id="img_images_3357.svg_32"> for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\hat{S}{(Q\mid S)R_{\text{ts}}(Q\mid P)},\)" src="images/6768.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 19.276ex; height: 2.993ex;" id="img_images_6768.svg"> (1) becomes
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{aligned} P&amp;\in \mu  &amp;\qquad\text{(1)},\\ \text{while (2) becomes}\qquad\qquad\qquad S\in \mu \ldotp \supset &amp;\ldotp S\mid R\in \mu  &amp;\qquad\text{(2)}. \end{aligned} \]" src="images/6769.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 62.054ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_6769.svg"></span></p>

<p>But by <a href="#_91_11" class="pginternal">*91·11</a>, writing <img alt="" data-tex="\(T\)" src="images/533.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.593ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_533.svg_17"> for the <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_79"> of *91·11, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_80"> for the
<img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/2826.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_2826.svg_13">, we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ TR_{\text{ts}}P\ldotp \supset \colon\ldotp S\in \mu \ldotp \supset _{S}\ldotp S\mid R\in \mu :P\in \mu :\supset \ldotp T\in\mu \ldotp \]" src="images/6770.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 49.092ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_6770.svg"></span></p>

<p>Hence, by (1) and (2), <img alt="" data-tex="\(TR_{\text{ts}}P.\supset.T\in \mu\)" src="images/6771.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.489ex; width: 15.945ex; height: 2.034ex;" id="img_images_6771.svg">, <i>i.e</i>.
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ TR_{\text{ts}}P.\supset.(Q\mid T)R_{\text{ts}}(Q\mid P), \]" src="images/6772.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 28.171ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6772.svg"></span>
which is the proposition to be proved.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*91·283.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:\mid Rʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻR\subset \text{Pot}ʻR \quad[\text{*91·282}]\)" src="images/6789.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 34.908ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6789.svg"></p>

<p>The following propositions show that the relative product of two powers
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_315"> is commutative, <i>i.e.</i> (cf. <a href="#_91_34" class="pginternal">*91·34</a>)
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P,\,Q\in \text{Potid}ʻR.\supset.P\mid Q=Q\mid P. \]" src="images/6790.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 34.32ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_6790.svg"></span></p>

<p>We also have (cf. <a href="#_91_341" class="pginternal">*91·341</a>)
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ P,\,Q\in \text{Potid}ʻR.\supset.P\mid Q\in \text{Potid}ʻR. \]" src="images/6791.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 37.207ex; height: 2.26ex;" id="img_images_6791.svg"></span></p>

<p>It is these propositions (as will appear in the sequel) which are the
source of the commutative law for the addition of finite ordinals.
Ordinals in general are not commutative, just as relative products
in general are not commutative; but owing to the fact that relative
products whose factors are powers of a given relation are commutative,
<i>finite</i> ordinals are commutative.</p>

<p>This formula should be compared with <a href="#_90_11" class="pginternal">*90·11</a>, in which an
analogous formula is given for <img alt="" data-tex="\(R_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6488.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.283ex; width: 2.705ex; height: 1.829ex;" id="img_images_6488.svg_11">. It will
be observed that here we do not require to add <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\in CʻR\)" src="images/6881.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.854ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6881.svg">,
for if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}ʻx=\Lambda\)" src="images/6882.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.69ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6882.svg">, the above formula leads
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(xR_{\text{po}}y.\supset.y\in \Lambda\)" src="images/6883.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 15.214ex; height: 2.27ex;" id="img_images_6883.svg">, <i>i.e.</i> to
<img alt="" data-tex="\({\sim}(xR_{\text{po}}y)\)" src="images/6884.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 9.517ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6884.svg">. Hence <img alt="" data-tex="\(xR_{\text{po}}y.\supset.\exists!\overleftarrow{R}ʻx\)" src="images/6885.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 16.759ex; height: 3.84ex;" id="img_images_6885.svg">,
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(xR_{\text{po}}y.\supset.x\in\text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/6886.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 18.633ex; height: 2.347ex;" id="img_images_6886.svg">.
It will be observed that <img alt="" data-tex="\(xR_{\text{po}}y\)" src="images/6528.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 5.997ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_6528.svg_1"> holds whenever <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_272">
belongs to every hereditary class which contains the immediate
successors of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_566">, whereas <img alt="" data-tex="\(xR_{\unicode{x2217}}y\)" src="images/6887.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 5.108ex; height: 2.009ex;" id="img_images_6887.svg"> holds whenever
<img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_273"> belongs to every hereditary class to which <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_567"> itself belongs.</p>

otherwise the powers from a certain point onwards form a cyclic series.</p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_601">[Pg 601]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_92">*92. POWERS OF ONE-MANY AND MANY-ONE RELATIONS.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *92.</p>

<p>If <img alt="" data-tex="\(R \in \text{Cls} \rightarrow 1\)" src="images/5271.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 12.288ex; height: 1.686ex;" id="img_images_5271.svg_1">, it follows that, starting from
a given term <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_568">, there is only one series of terms <img alt="" data-tex="\(x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, \ldots\)" src="images/6906.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 12.515ex; height: 1.439ex;" id="img_images_6906.svg">
such that
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ x R x_{1} . x_{1} R x_{2} . x_{2} R x_{3} . \ldots \text{.} \]" src="images/6907.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 24.53ex; height: 1.92ex;" id="img_images_6907.svg"></span></p>

<p>Thus for example the relation of son to father is a <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Cls}\rightarrow 1\)" src="images/6908.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 7.804ex; height: 1.643ex;" id="img_images_6908.svg">;
and starting from a given man, the series of ancestors
in the direct male line (which is the above series <img alt="" data-tex="\(x_{1}\)" src="images/3400.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.282ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_3400.svg_2">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x_{2}\)" src="images/3401.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 2.282ex; height: 1.339ex;" id="img_images_3401.svg_2">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(x_{3}\)" src="images/3402.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.375ex; width: 2.282ex; height: 1.375ex;" id="img_images_3402.svg_2">,...) is unique and determinate. A result of this
property of many-one relations is that if, starting from a term <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_274">,
we go backwards a certain number of steps to a term <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_569">, and then
forward a greater number of steps to a term <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_56">, we must pass through
<img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_275"> in going from <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_570"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_57">; while if the number of steps from
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_571"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_58"> is less than that from <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_572"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_276">, <img alt="" data-tex="\(z\)" src="images/228.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.052ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_228.svg_59"> must lie
on the road from <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_573"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_277">. These facts are expressed by the
proposition:
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ R \in \text{Cls} \rightarrow 1 .\supset. \breve{R}_{\unicode{x2217}} \mid R_{\unicode{x2217}} \unicode{x2abd} R_{\unicode{x2217}}     \unicode{x228d}  \breve{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}\text{.} \]" src="images/6909.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 32.109ex; height: 2.977ex;" id="img_images_6909.svg"></span></p>

<p>In the present number, we have to establish various propositions of
this kind.</p>

<p>We prove in this number various propositions which are used in the
discussion of "families" in <a href="#_96" class="pginternal">*96</a> and <a href="#_97" class="pginternal">*97</a>, and some which are used in
the theory of finite and infinite. But on the whole the propositions
of this number are not much used. The most important of them are the
following:</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*92·11.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: R \in 1 \rightarrow \text{Cls} .\supset. R_{\text{po}} \mid \breve{R} \unicode{x2abd} R_{\unicode{x2217}} . R_{\text{po}}     \mid \breve{R} = R_{\unicode{x2217}} \upharpoonright \text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/6910.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 50.888ex; height: 3.064ex;" id="img_images_6910.svg"></p>

<p>with a similar proposition (<a href="#_92_111" class="pginternal">*92·111</a>) for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Cls} \rightarrow 1\)" src="images/4961.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 7.804ex; height: 1.643ex;" id="img_images_4961.svg_5">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*92·132.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: R \in 1 \rightarrow \text{Cls} . Q,\,T \in \text{Potid}ʻR .\supset. Q \mid T \mid \breve{Q} \unicode{x2abd} T\)" src="images/6911.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 47.645ex; height: 3.025ex;" id="img_images_6911.svg"></p>

<p>with a similar proposition (<a href="#_92_133" class="pginternal">*92·133</a>) for <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{Cls} \rightarrow 1\)" src="images/4961.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 7.804ex; height: 1.643ex;" id="img_images_4961.svg_6">.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*92·14.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: \text{ᗡ}ʻR \subset \text{D}ʻR . Q \in \text{Pot}ʻR .\supset. \text{D}ʻQ = \text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/6912.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 43.549ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6912.svg"></p>

<p>On this proposition, compare the remarks on <a href="#_91_271" class="pginternal">*91·271</a> in the introduction
to <a href="#_91" class="pginternal">*91</a>. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_318"> is a serial relation, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR \subset \text{D}ʻR\)" src="images/6913.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.252ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6913.svg"> is the condition that the series may have no last term.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*92·31.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: R \in 1 \rightarrow \text{Cls} .\supset. R_{\unicode{x2217}} \mid \breve{R}_{\unicode{x2217}} = R_{\unicode{x2217}}     \unicode{x228d}  \breve{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6914.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 35.78ex; height: 2.977ex;" id="img_images_6914.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*92·311.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: R \in \text{Cls} \rightarrow 1 .\supset. \breve{R}_{\unicode{x2217}} \mid R_{\unicode{x2217}} = R_{\unicode{x2217}}     \unicode{x228d}  \breve{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/6915.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.563ex; width: 35.78ex; height: 2.977ex;" id="img_images_6915.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*92·1.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:R\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}.\supset.\text{Potid}ʻR\subset 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}\)" src="images/6916.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 38.035ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6916.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*72·17.*71·26}.&amp;\supset\vdash.I\upharpoonright CʻR\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls} &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{*71·25}. &amp;\supset\vdash\colon\ldotp \text{Hp}.\supset:S\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}.\supset.SʻR\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls} &amp;\qquad \text{(2)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).(2).*91·17}.\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/6917.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.733ex; width: 80.666ex; height: 8.597ex;" id="img_images_6917.svg"></span></p>

<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_607">[Pg 607]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_93">*93. INDUCTIVE ANALYSIS OF THE FIELD OF A RELATION.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *93.</p>

<p>For this number, we introduce three new notations, of which the first
two will be used constantly, especially in the theory of series, while
the third will be seldom used except in the present section. The two
which are constantly used are
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ xBP, ~ \text{meaning} ~ x \in \text{D}ʻP - \text{ᗡ}ʻP \]" src="images/6975.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 31.169ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_6975.svg"></span>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{and} \quad x \mathop{\text{min}_{P}} \alpha, ~ \text{meaning} ~ x \in \alpha \cap CʻP-\breve{P}ʻʻ\alpha\text{,} \]" src="images/6976.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 47.055ex; height: 2.88ex;" id="img_images_6976.svg"></span>
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_574"> is a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_322"> and of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/3399.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3399.svg_8">, and no member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_323"> precedes <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_575"> in <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/3399.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3399.svg_9">.</p>

<p>The letter <img alt="" data-tex="\(B\)" src="images/41.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_41.svg_3"> may be regarded as standing for "begins." Thus if we
take any member <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_278"> of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/3399.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3399.svg_10">, and proceed backwards and forwards as
far as possible by <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_82">-steps, we obtain a series which may be called
the "family" of <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_279">: this series, if it has a first term, has one
which is a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP\)" src="images/6531.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.965ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6531.svg_2">; thus the members of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{D}ʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP\)" src="images/6531.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 11.965ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6531.svg_3"> are the beginners of families. For example,
if <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_83"> is the relation of a peer to his heir, "<img alt="" data-tex="\(xBP\)" src="images/6548.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 4.71ex; height: 1.57ex;" id="img_images_6548.svg_2">" will mean
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_576"> is a peer who is not the heir of a peer"; thus <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_577"> is the
first of his family. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_84"> is the relation of parent and child,
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(xBP\)" src="images/6548.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 4.71ex; height: 1.57ex;" id="img_images_6548.svg_3">" will be satisfied only by Adam and Eve; and so for other
relations.</p>

<p>The definition of <img alt="" data-tex="\(B\)" src="images/41.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_41.svg_4"> is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ B = \hat{x}\hat{P}(x \in \text{D}ʻP - \text{ᗡ}ʻP) \quad \text{Df}\text{.} \]" src="images/6977.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 30.825ex; height: 2.943ex;" id="img_images_6977.svg"></span>
Hence <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{B}ʻP = \text{D}ʻP - \text{ᗡ}ʻP\)" src="images/6978.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 19.756ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6978.svg">. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_85"> is
the generating relation of a series which has a first term, that first
term is <img alt="" data-tex="\(BʻP\)" src="images/6550.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6550.svg_2">; if there is a last term it is <img alt="" data-tex="\(Bʻ\breve{P}\)" src="images/6552.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 2.867ex;" id="img_images_6552.svg_1">.</p>

<p>If <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_324"> is any class, we may call a term <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_578"> a <i>minimum</i>
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_325"> with respect to <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_86"> if it is a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_326"> and
of <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/3399.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3399.svg_11">, but does not follow any member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_327">, <i>i.e.</i>
is not a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{P}ʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6979.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 5.862ex; height: 2.867ex;" id="img_images_6979.svg">. We denote this relation of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_579"> to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_328"> by "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{min}_{P}\)" src="images/6536.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 5.161ex; height: 1.853ex;" id="img_images_6536.svg_4">"; thus we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ x \mathop{\text{min}_{P}} \alpha .\equiv. x \in \alpha \cap CʻP - \breve{P}ʻʻ\alpha\text{,} \]" src="images/6980.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 34.484ex; height: 2.867ex;" id="img_images_6980.svg"></span>
and the definition of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{min}_{P}\)" src="images/6536.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 5.161ex; height: 1.853ex;" id="img_images_6536.svg_5"> is
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{min}_{P} = \hat{x}\hat{\alpha}(x \in \alpha \cap CʻP - \breve{P}ʻʻ\alpha) \quad \text{Df}\text{.} \]" src="images/6981.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 39.419ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_6981.svg"></span></p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_608">[Pg 608]</span></p>

<p>We shall also, when convenient, write "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{min}(P)\)" src="images/6982.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 7.231ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_6982.svg">" in place of
"<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{min}_{P}\)" src="images/6536.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 5.161ex; height: 1.853ex;" id="img_images_6536.svg_6">."</p>

<p>We have <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻ\alpha = \alpha \cap CʻP - \breve{P}ʻʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6983.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 28.35ex; height: 3.934ex;" id="img_images_6983.svg">.</p>

<p>If <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_87"> is serial, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{min}}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6540.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.966ex; height: 3.934ex;" id="img_images_6540.svg_1"> reduces
to a single term if it is not null; thus if a class <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_329"> has a
first term, this term is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{min}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6542.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.966ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6542.svg_1">. We also put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{max}_{P} = \text{min}(\breve{P}) \quad \text{Df}\text{,} \]" src="images/6984.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 21.16ex; height: 2.98ex;" id="img_images_6984.svg"></span>
and then <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6985.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.405ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6985.svg">, if it exists, is the last
term of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_330"> in the <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_88">-series. Thus if <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_331">
is the class of peers, and <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_89"> is the relation of father
to son, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{min}_{P}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6986.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.966ex; height: 3.934ex;" id="img_images_6986.svg"> consists
of those peers who are the first of their line, while
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{max}_{P}}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6987.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.405ex; height: 3.434ex;" id="img_images_6987.svg"> consists of those peers who
are the last of their line. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_332"> is a class of numbers, and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_90"> is the relation of less to greater, <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{min}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6542.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 7.966ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6542.svg_2">
is the smallest member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\alpha\)" src="images/209.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.448ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_209.svg_333"> (if it exists), and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{max}_{P}ʻ\alpha\)" src="images/6985.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.405ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6985.svg_1"> is the largest (if it exists).</p>

<p><img alt="" data-tex="\(B\)" src="images/41.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_41.svg_5"> and "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{max}_{P}\)" src="images/6988.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 5.6ex; height: 1.353ex;" id="img_images_6988.svg">" and "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{min}_{P}\)" src="images/6536.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 5.161ex; height: 1.853ex;" id="img_images_6536.svg_7">" will be used constantly in connection with
series, where the two latter will be considered in detail, but the present number
is more specially concerned with a less general idea, namely that of <i>generations</i>.
Take, <i>e.g.</i>, the relation of parent and child; let us call it <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_91">. Then
the first generation consists of those who are parents but not children,
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/6551.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6551.svg_3">; the second consists of those who are children but not grandchildren,
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻP - \text{ᗡ}ʻP^{2}\)" src="images/6989.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.707ex; height: 2.339ex;" id="img_images_6989.svg">, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻP - \breve{P}ʻʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻP\)" src="images/6990.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 16.008ex; height: 2.867ex;" id="img_images_6990.svg">, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{min}_{P}}ʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻP\)" src="images/6991.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.932ex; height: 3.934ex;" id="img_images_6991.svg">;
    the third consists of those
who are grandchildren but not great-grandchildren, <i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻP^{2} - \text{ᗡ}ʻP^{3}\)" src="images/6992.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.82ex; height: 2.339ex;" id="img_images_6992.svg">, <i>i.e.</i>
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻP^{2} - \breve{P}ʻʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻP^{2}\)" src="images/6993.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 18.234ex; height: 2.867ex;" id="img_images_6993.svg">, <i>i.e.</i>
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{min}_{P}}ʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻP^{2}\)" src="images/6994.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.045ex; height: 3.934ex;" id="img_images_6994.svg">; and so on. Also we
have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \overrightarrow{B}ʻP = \overrightarrow{\text{min}_{P}}ʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻ(I \upharpoonright CʻP)\text{;} \]" src="images/6995.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 27.53ex; height: 4.048ex;" id="img_images_6995.svg"></span>
hence the generations of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_92"> are
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{\text{min}_{P}}ʻʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Potid}ʻP\)" src="images/6996.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 20.444ex; height: 3.934ex;" id="img_images_6996.svg">. Thus we
put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \text{gen}ʻP = \overrightarrow{\text{min}_{P}}ʻʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Potid}ʻP \quad \text{Df}\text{,} \]" src="images/6997.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 35.223ex; height: 3.948ex;" id="img_images_6997.svg"></span>
where "<img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{gen}\)" src="images/6547.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 3.394ex; height: 1.491ex;" id="img_images_6547.svg_1">" stands for "generation."</p>

<p>When <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_93"> is a one-many relation, such as that of father and son,
every generation is of the form <img alt="" data-tex="\(\breve{T}ʻʻ\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/6556.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 9.081ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6556.svg_1">,
where <img alt="" data-tex="\(T\)" src="images/533.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.593ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_533.svg_18"> is a power of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_94"> (including <img alt="" data-tex="\(I \upharpoonright CʻP\)" src="images/6998.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 8.117ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6998.svg">).
When <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_95"> is not a one-many relation, this is not in general the case.</p>

<p>The generations of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_96"> do not in general exhaust the field of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_97">. For <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_580"> will only belong to a generation of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_98"> if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_581">
can be reached by successive <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_99">-steps starting from a member of
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/6551.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.774ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6551.svg_4">. If some of the families constituting the
field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_100"> have no beginning, the members of these families will
not belong to any generation of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_101">. Such terms together constitute
the class
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{align} &amp;pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP,\\ \text{or} \quad &amp;pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Potid}ʻP,\\ \end{align} \]" src="images/6999.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.036ex; width: 19.973ex; height: 5.204ex;" id="img_images_6999.svg"></span>
which is the same class.</p>

<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_609">[Pg 609]</span></p>

<p>Thus the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_102"> may be divided into two mutually exclusive
portions, <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\text{gen}ʻP\)" src="images/6558.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 8.869ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_6558.svg_1"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\)" src="images/6557.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.176ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6557.svg_2">.</p>

<p>The present number begins with some elementary properties of <img alt="" data-tex="\(B\)" src="images/41.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_41.svg_6">
and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{min}_{P}\)" src="images/6536.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 5.161ex; height: 1.853ex;" id="img_images_6536.svg_8"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{max}_{P}\)" src="images/6988.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.339ex; width: 5.6ex; height: 1.353ex;" id="img_images_6988.svg_1">. We then (<a href="#_93_2" class="pginternal">*93·2</a>—<a href="#_93_275" class="pginternal">·275</a>)
consider such properties of generations as do not demand any hypothesis
as to <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_103">. We prove</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·25.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\text{gen}ʻP\in \text{Cls}^{2}\,\text{excl}\)" src="images/7000.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 19.957ex; height: 2.509ex;" id="img_images_7000.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·261.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP=pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Potid}ʻP.pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\subset \text{ᗡ}ʻP\)" src="images/7001.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 55.259ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7001.svg"></p>

<p>and we prove (*93·274·275) that <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\text{gen}ʻP\)" src="images/6558.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 8.869ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_6558.svg_2"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\)" src="images/6557.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.176ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6557.svg_3"> are mutually exclusive, and together
constitute <img alt="" data-tex="\(CʻP\)" src="images/3399.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.776ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_3399.svg_12">. We then proceed to a set of propositions
(<a href="#_93_3" class="pginternal">*93·3</a>—<a href="#_93_41" class="pginternal">·41</a>) demanding that P should be one-many or many-one or
one-one. We prove</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·32.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp P\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}.\supset:\alpha\in \text{gen}ʻP.\equiv.(\exists T).T\in \text{Potid}ʻP.\alpha=\breve{T}ʻʻ\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/7002.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 67.148ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7002.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·36.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:P\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}.\supset.sʻ\text{gen}ʻP=\breve{P}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻ\overrightarrow{B}ʻP\)" src="images/7003.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 40.496ex; height: 3.656ex;" id="img_images_7003.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·381.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash\colon\ldotp P\in \text{Cls}\rightarrow 1.\supset:x\in pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻ\breve{P}.\equiv.\overleftarrow{P}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻx\subset     \text{D}ʻP.x\in CʻP\)" src="images/7004.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 64.867ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_7004.svg"></p>

<p>and various other properties of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{gen}ʻP\)" src="images/7005.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 6.45ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_7005.svg"> and
<img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\)" src="images/6557.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.176ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_6557.svg_4"> when <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\in 1\rightarrow \text{Cls}\)" src="images/6555.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 12.269ex; height: 1.686ex;" id="img_images_6555.svg_1">.</p>

<p>The propositions of this number are used throughout the rest of this
section; they are also used in the cardinal theory of finite and
infinite. The early propositions, down to <a href="#_93_12" class="pginternal">*93·12</a> inclusive, are also
used in the theory of series.</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·1.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:xBP.\equiv.x\in \text{D}ʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP \quad[\text{*21·3.(*93·01)}]\)" src="images/7010.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 44.496ex; height: 2.262ex;" id="img_images_7010.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·101.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\overrightarrow{B}ʻP=\text{D}ʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP \quad[\text{*93·1.*32·18}]\)" src="images/7011.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 37.732ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7011.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·102.</b> <span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[\begin{align}&amp;\vdash:x=BʻP.\equiv.x=\breve{\iota}ʻ(\text{D}ʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP).\equiv.\text{D}ʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP\in 1.x\in \text{D}ʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP\\ &amp;[\text{*93·101.*53·4}]\end{align}\]" src="images/7012.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.122ex; width: 72.608ex; height: 5.376ex;" id="img_images_7012.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·103.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.\overrightarrow{B}ʻP=CʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP\)" src="images/7013.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 22.135ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_7013.svg"></p>

<p><i>Dem.</i></p>

<p><span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} \vdash.\text{*22·9.*33·16}.&amp;\supset\vdash.CʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP=\text{D}ʻP-\text{ᗡ}ʻP &amp;\qquad \text{(1)}\\ \vdash.\text{(1).*93·101}. &amp;\supset\vdash.\text{Prop} \end{array} \]" src="images/7014.svg" style="vertical-align: -2.149ex; width: 58.113ex; height: 5.43ex;" id="img_images_7014.svg"></span></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·54.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:S\in \text{Pot}ʻP.xSx.\supset.x\in pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\)" src="images/7084.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 39.536ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7084.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·55.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash.Cʻ(P_{\text{po}}\dot{\cap}I)\subset pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\)" src="images/7085.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 29.398ex; height: 2.738ex;" id="img_images_7085.svg"></p>

<p class="nind"><b>*93·56.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash:\dot{\exists}!(P_{\text{po}}\dot{\cap}I).\supset.\exists !pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻP\)" src="images/7086.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 31.101ex; height: 2.955ex;" id="img_images_7086.svg"></p>
