<div class="chapter">
<p><span class="pagenum" id="Page_654">[Pg 654]</span></p>
<h2 class="nobreak" id="_97">*97. ANALYSIS OF THE FIELD OF A RELATION INTO FAMILIES.</h2>
</div>


<p><i>Summary of</i> *97.</p>

<p>In this number, we consider not only the posterity
of a term, but the ancestry and posterity together,
<i>i.e.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻx \cup\overleftarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻx\)" src="images/7488.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.961ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_7488.svg">.
We put
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \overleftrightarrow{R}ʻx = \overrightarrow{R}ʻx \cup (\iotaʻx \cap CʻR) \cup \overleftarrow{R}ʻx \quad \text{Df}\text{.} \]" src="images/7489.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 40.454ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7489.svg"></span></p>

<p>Thus the whole family of a term, <i>i.e.</i> its ancestry and posterity
together, is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻx\)" src="images/6578.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.09ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6578.svg_1">. The most
important case here is when <img alt="" data-tex="\(R \in 1 \rightarrow 1\)" src="images/5064.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 10.265ex; height: 1.636ex;" id="img_images_5064.svg_1">; in this case
families are mutually exclusive, <i>i.e.</i> we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash: R \in 1 \rightarrow 1 .\supset. \overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻCʻR \in \text{Cls} ~ \text{ex}^{2} ~ \text{excl}\text{.} \]" src="images/7490.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 42.324ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_7490.svg"></span></p>

<p>In case <img alt="" data-tex="\(R \in 1 \rightarrow 1\)" src="images/5064.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 10.265ex; height: 1.636ex;" id="img_images_5064.svg_2"> and <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_294"> belongs to
a family which has a beginning, <i>i.e.</i> in case
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\exists!\overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻy \cap \overrightarrow{B}ʻR\)" src="images/7491.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 15.098ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_7491.svg">, the whole family of <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_295"> consists of the
posterity of the beginning, <i>i.e.</i> we have
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \vdash: R \in 1 \rightarrow 1 . xBR . x R_{\unicode{x2217}} y .\supset. \overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻy = \overleftarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻx\text{,} \]" src="images/7492.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 44.166ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_7492.svg"></span>
whence</p>

<p class="nind"><b>*97·21.</b> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\vdash: R \in 1 \rightarrow 1 .\supset. \overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻsʻ\text{gen}ʻR = \overleftarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻ\overrightarrow{B}ʻR\)" src="images/7493.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 45.68ex; height: 3.656ex;" id="img_images_7493.svg"></p>

<figure class="figcenter width500" style="width: 894px;" id="i_654">
<img alt="A grid of dots where an oval enclosed some dots showing field mapping." height="500" src="images/i_654.jpg" width="894" id="img_images_i_654.jpg">
</figure>


<p>When <img alt="" data-tex="\(R \in 1 \rightarrow 1\)" src="images/5064.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 10.265ex; height: 1.636ex;" id="img_images_5064.svg_3">, the relation of <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{gen}ʻR\)" src="images/6583.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 6.468ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_6583.svg_1">
to <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻ\overrightarrow{B}ʻR\)" src="images/6581.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 10.945ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6581.svg_3">
may be pictured as the relation of rows to columns. <i>E.g.</i>
let the field of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_343"> consist of the dots in the accompanying
rectangle, and let each dot have the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_344"> to the dot
below it. Then the top row is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overrightarrow{B}ʻR\)" src="images/6580.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 4.792ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6580.svg_1">, the second
<span class="pagenum" id="Page_655">[Pg 655]</span>row is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR - \text{ᗡ}ʻR^{2}\)" src="images/7494.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 12.618ex; height: 2.339ex;" id="img_images_7494.svg">, the third is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\text{ᗡ}ʻR^{2} - \text{ᗡ}ʻR^{3}\)" src="images/7495.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.605ex; height: 2.339ex;" id="img_images_7495.svg">,
and so on; thus the rows are the generations of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_345">. Again,
if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_595"> is any dot in the top row, the column beginning
with <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_596"> is <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻx\)" src="images/6570.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.09ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6570.svg_22">,
and if <img alt="" data-tex="\(y\)" src="images/141.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 1.109ex; height: 1.464ex;" id="img_images_141.svg_296"> is any member of this column, the column is
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻy\)" src="images/7496.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.464ex; width: 5.905ex; height: 3.654ex;" id="img_images_7496.svg">. Thus the columns are
the families of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_346">. It will be seen that in the case represented
by the above figure, every family consists of a selection from the
generations, and every generation consists of a selection from the
families, <i>i.e.</i>
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \overleftarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻ\overrightarrow{B}ʻR \subset \text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\text{gen}ʻR     . \text{gen}ʻR \subset \text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\overleftarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻ\overrightarrow{B}ʻR\text{.} \]" src="images/7497.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 60.157ex; height: 3.656ex;" id="img_images_7497.svg"></span></p>

<p>The circumstances under which this occurs will be considered in the
present number (<a href="#_97_3" class="pginternal">*97·3</a>—<a href="#_97_47" class="pginternal">·47</a>). The results are summed up in <a href="#_97_47" class="pginternal">*97·47</a>.</p>

<p>The remaining propositions (<a href="#_97_5" class="pginternal">*97·5</a>—<a href="#_97_58" class="pginternal">·58</a>) are concerned with
<i>circular</i> families of one-one relations. If <img alt="" data-tex="\(R \in 1 \rightarrow 1\)" src="images/5064.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.09ex; width: 10.265ex; height: 1.636ex;" id="img_images_5064.svg_4">,
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻx\)" src="images/6578.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 6.09ex; height: 3.643ex;" id="img_images_6578.svg_2"> is a
circular family if <img alt="" data-tex="\(x R_{\text{po}} x\)" src="images/7498.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 6.183ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_7498.svg">. In that case, we have
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x R_{\text{po}} y .\supset. y R_{\text{po}} x\)" src="images/7499.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 15.766ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_7499.svg">; moreover there is a
definite power of <img alt="" data-tex="\(R\)" src="images/31.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 1.717ex; height: 1.593ex;" id="img_images_31.svg_347">, say <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_112">, such that every member of the
family of <img alt="" data-tex="\(x\)" src="images/30.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.294ex; height: 1.025ex;" id="img_images_30.svg_597"> has the relation <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_113"> to itself (<a href="#_97_54" class="pginternal">*97·54</a>). (The same
will hold, of course, of all powers of <img alt="" data-tex="\(P\)" src="images/384.svg" style="vertical-align: 0; width: 1.699ex; height: 1.545ex;" id="img_images_384.svg_114">.) The families of a
<img alt="" data-tex="\(1 \rightarrow 1\)" src="images/4959.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 5.782ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_4959.svg_7"> are all either circular or open, <i>i.e.</i> we have
(<a href="#_97_55" class="pginternal">*97·55</a>) either <img alt="" data-tex="\(y \in \overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻx .\supset_{y}. y R_{\text{po}} y\)" src="images/7500.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.667ex; width: 20.52ex; height: 3.857ex;" id="img_images_7500.svg">,
or <img alt="" data-tex="\(y \in \overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻx .\supset_{y}. {\sim}(y R_{\text{po}} y)\)" src="images/7501.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.667ex; width: 24.041ex; height: 3.857ex;" id="img_images_7501.svg">.
The <img alt="" data-tex="\(Q\)" src="images/2826.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.439ex; width: 1.79ex; height: 2.032ex;" id="img_images_2826.svg_24">-shaped families considered in <a href="#_96" class="pginternal">*96</a> are
not possible for a <img alt="" data-tex="\(1 \rightarrow 1\)" src="images/4959.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 5.782ex; height: 1.532ex;" id="img_images_4959.svg_8">, since in such families the
term at the junction of the tail and the circle has two predecessors.
The family of any member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\text{gen}ʻR\)" src="images/7502.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 8.887ex; height: 2.163ex;" id="img_images_7502.svg"> must be open (<a href="#_97_57" class="pginternal">*97·57</a>).
The family of a member of <img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻR\)" src="images/7503.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 13.195ex; height: 2.149ex;" id="img_images_7503.svg"> need not be
closed, but cannot have a beginning; if open, it forms a series of
type <img alt="" data-tex="\(^{\unicode{x2217}}\omega\)" src="images/7504.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 2.395ex; height: 1.59ex;" id="img_images_7504.svg"> or <img alt="" data-tex="\({}^{\unicode{x2217}}\omega + \omega\)" src="images/7505.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 6.568ex; height: 1.751ex;" id="img_images_7505.svg">,
according as it has or has not an end<a class="fnanchor pginternal" href="#Footnote_68" id="FNanchor_68">[68]</a>.
Finite open families are contained in <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\text{gen}ʻR \cap sʻ\text{gen}ʻ\breve{R}\)" src="images/7506.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 20.288ex; height: 2.88ex;" id="img_images_7506.svg">; families of type <img alt="" data-tex="\(\omega\)" src="images/52.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 1.407ex; height: 1.027ex;" id="img_images_52.svg_2"> are contained
in <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\text{gen}ʻR \cap pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻ\breve{R}\)" src="images/7507.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 24.596ex; height: 2.88ex;" id="img_images_7507.svg">; those of
type <img alt="" data-tex="\({}^{\unicode{x2217}}\omega\)" src="images/7508.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.025ex; width: 2.395ex; height: 1.59ex;" id="img_images_7508.svg">, in <img alt="" data-tex="\(sʻ\text{gen}ʻ\breve{R} \cap pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻR\)" src="images/7509.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.466ex; width: 24.596ex; height: 2.88ex;" id="img_images_7509.svg">;
those of type <img alt="" data-tex="\({}^{\unicode{x2217}}\omega + \omega\)" src="images/7505.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 6.568ex; height: 1.751ex;" id="img_images_7505.svg_1">
and circular families are contained in
<img alt="" data-tex="\(pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻR \cap pʻ\text{ᗡ}ʻʻ\text{Pot}ʻ\breve{R}\)" src="images/7510.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.452ex; width: 28.904ex; height: 2.867ex;" id="img_images_7510.svg">.
Those of type <img alt="" data-tex="\(^{\unicode{x2217}}\omega + \omega\)" src="images/7511.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.186ex; width: 6.568ex; height: 1.751ex;" id="img_images_7511.svg"> are distinguished
from circular families by the fact that in the former we do not have
<img alt="" data-tex="\(x R_{\text{po}} x\)" src="images/7498.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.65ex; width: 6.183ex; height: 2.195ex;" id="img_images_7498.svg_1">, while in the latter we do have this.</p>

propositions of the present number are the following:</p>

<p><i>Note.</i> <img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/7531.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.283ex; width: 3.439ex; height: 3.473ex;" id="img_images_7531.svg"> is to mean (<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}})\)" src="images/7532.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 4.319ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7532.svg">, not (<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftrightarrow{R})_{\unicode{x2217}}\)" src="images/7533.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.566ex; width: 4.319ex; height: 3.756ex;" id="img_images_7533.svg">.
    The latter is unmeaning, since
<img alt="" data-tex="\(\overleftrightarrow{R}\)" src="images/7534.svg" style="vertical-align: -0.048ex; width: 2.451ex; height: 3.238ex;" id="img_images_7534.svg"> is never a homogeneous relation, and therefore its square and higher
powers are unmeaning.</p>

<p>The remaining propositions of this number (except <a href="#_97_5" class="pginternal">*97·5</a> ff.) are
concerned with proving that, under certain hypotheses,
<span class="align-center"><img alt="" data-tex="\[ \begin{array}{l} &amp;\overleftarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻ\overrightarrow{B}ʻR\subset \text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\text{gen}ʻR,\,\, \textit{i.e.}\,\, \overleftrightarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻsʻ\text{gen}ʻR\subset     \text{D}ʻʻ{\in}_{\Delta}ʻ\text{gen}ʻR,\\ \text{and}  &amp;\qquad\qquad\text{gen}ʻR-\iotaʻ\Lambda\subset \text{D}ʻʻ\overleftarrow{R}_{\unicode{x2217}}ʻʻ\overrightarrow{B}ʻR. \end{array} \]" src="images/7559.svg" style="vertical-align: -3.643ex; width: 74.897ex; height: 8.416ex;" id="img_images_7559.svg"></span></p>

<p>These propositions have the merit of proving the existence of
selections in the cases to which they apply.</p>
